characters.name: Elle
characters.description: Babies Ever After:After Morty reuses the VR helmet in an attempt to see Elle again, he finds a dimension where he and Elle manage to get married and have a daughter together named Maria Smith. Cute Monster Girl: In Mullet Rick's universe, she doesn't look completely human, instead having green skin with blue stripes, white hair, and red eyes with no pupils. Deconstructed Character Archetype: Elle is a deconstruction of theMagical Girlfriendarchetype popular in Japanese anime and manga. One day, using a virtual reality system, Morty Smith meets a mysterious girl named Elle, who claims to know Morty. He instantly falls in love with her, tries to find her, and eventually finds her in real life. The two of them get together and become a couple, with her moving into his home. Elle is revealed to be a member of a time-traveling race that could predict the future, and the Galactic Federation wiped out her race. Even though she just met him, Elle appears to be genuinely in love with Morty. It is later revealed that Elle is actuallyfrom an alternate dimension, where she falls in love with that version of Morty. Through her support, her Morty, who is named Space Morty, became a galactic hero but tragically died. Elle, despite her time powers, cannot prevent his death. Elle is stuck in a time loop of watching Space Morty die and eventually escapes to the main Morty's dimension, where she can be with another version of her love.Elle appears to be the typical magical girlfriend, and she’s in love with the main male character despitenot having a reason to love him other than him being a nice guy who appears to be improving his life. But she becomes a dark destruction when it’s revealed that she loves Morty because she was in love with an alternate version of him, and she is just projecting her feelings for that version of Morty to the Main Morty.It was later revealed thatto stop the time loop, Elle is willing to destroy her old universe along with all the good she did with her ve

characters.name: Mullet Rick
characters.description: A Mortyless Rick who is familiar with Elle. Outliving One's Offspring: He says in the first episode that his Morty is dead.His Morty being Space Morty.

characters.name: Space Morty
characters.description: The Hero: He fought on the front lines against the tyrannical Galactic Federation. The Lost Lenore:All versions of Elle were in love with him, but having to see him die every time very slowly pushed main Elle to find a way to end the cycle to stop getting her heart broken. Posthumous Character:All of his scenes are flashbacks, and he bites the dust in Episode 7, which also reveals he's Mullet Rick's grandson. Too Good for This Sinful Earth:He always died by some random Galactic Federation soldiers seeking to claim the bounty on his head.

characters.name: Frank
characters.description: A friendly businessman whom Morty meets many, many times during his VR adventures(actually a real man from many dimensions)who formed a close relationship with him. Ambiguously Bi: Many several instances of him and Morty could've been seen as Frank having strong romantic feelings for him. On the instances where Morty couldn't find Elle, he does end up eloping with Frank instead. Nice Guy: He was just a stranger who really was out to help Morty in any way he could to make his life all the better. One-Steve Limit: Frank shares the first name with the character Frank Palicky from the pilot episode of the cartoon. Outside of their first names, the two characters are complete opposites, with Frank being a kind adult man while Frank Palicky is an unhinged teenage bully. Frank was Morty’s friend, while Frank Palicky was Morty’s bully. Frank only first appeared in the first episode of the anime but then appeared in the last episode and had a big role, while Frank Palicky was killed off in the first episode of the cartoon and has not been mentioned since.

characters.name: Beth Smith
characters.description: Jerry's wife, Summer and Morty's mother and Rick's daughter, Beth works as a veterinarian specializing in cardiothoracic surgery and faces the problems that follow her unstable marriage and her dad living with her family, though she's the least affected family member by the latter of the two. As the series goes on, it becomes increasingly clear she has some darker sides to her personality; both as a consequence of being Rick's daughter as well as issues stemming from his abandonment of her in her childhood. Abusive Parents:Downplayedas it is not really shown often and Beth is mostly shown to be a good mom but there are times where she is emotionally abusive to her son and daughter, as well as genuinely neglectful. Beth even admits at one point that deep down she doesn't have a "maternal instinct", and that she has to be especially encouraged to come to the aid of her children. Starting with the Season 3 finale, however, she seems to be making an effort to be a genuinely better parent. Actor Allusion: Her job as a horse surgeon is partially a reference to the fact that her actress' other most prominent role was asan actual doctor. Actually a Doombot:The end of season 3 seemed to suggest (though not confirm) that Beth had abandoned her family to travel the world/universe/multiverse to find herself while Rick created a clone of her programmed with all her memories and personality to take her place so no one would be the wiser and allow Beth the option to return to the family if she so desired. SeeA.I. Is a Crapshootfor more.Laterthe season 4 finale reveals that Rickdidend up cloning Beth resulting in two versions of her, one that stayed behind to raise her family and one that went off to have adventures. However, both Beths believe they're the original and both of them have bombs implanted in their necks, which Rick claims would transmit the memories of the Clone Beth into the original before vaporizing the clone. The end of the episode reveals not even Rick knows whic

characters.name: Jerry Smith
characters.description: Acquired Situational Narcissism: As shown in episodes like "Something Ricked This Way Comes" and "Childrick of Mort"; any time Jerry is shown genuine respect and admiration by a big enough group, he quickly lets it go to his head, becoming insufferably arrogant, selfish and doing whatever he can to hang on to his newfound popularity for as long as possible. A Lighter Shade of Black: When compared with the other adults in the Smith-Sanchez family. Jerry may not be as toxic or abusive as someone like Rick or Beth; but he can still be a selfish, immature jackass in his own right. Allergic to Routine:Inverted.Jerry craves structure and routine in his life, which adds further differences between him and Rick. In Season 3, when Earth was briefly taken over by an alien dictatorship, Jerry is happier and more fulfilled than he has ever been in his life. InThe Stingerfor one episode, when Jerry accidentally samples a substance that would allow him to experience his own idea of perfect existence, Jerry's ideal life is a water delivery man, who does nothing but drive around all day delivering and installing large jugs into water coolers. Alternate Self:If Summer and Morty weren't born, he would have a successful (albeit questionably earned) Hollywood career.In any timeline where Beth is in danger, he steps up to the plate to save her. "Rick Potion #9" is the only timeline where it has clearly stuck. If Summer and Morty weren't born, he would have a successful (albeit questionably earned) Hollywood career.

characters.name: Summer Smith
characters.description: The daughter of Jerry and Beth, the granddaughter of Rick, and the sister of Morty. Summer behaves the way a typical teenage daughter living in a house with a psychotic grandfather would and is considerably more level-headed than the two combined, but that doesn't mean she lacks her fair share of sass. Abusive Grandparents: The earlier seasons show Rick's treatment of Summer to be rather harsh. Compared to Rick's treatment of the rest of the Smith family, he doesn't value Summer's company as much as Morty, and he doesn't shower Summer with affection like he does with Beth. The only person in the family that Rick actively treats worse than Summer is Jerry, whom Rick has his reasons for disliking. Thankfully, Rick manages to undergo character development and softens his attitude towards Summer in later seasons. The Ace: Downplayed but Summer does exhibit hints of this trope, particularly in later seasons once she's given more screentime. It's shown in several episodes that Summer possesses superior intelligence, she's a surprisingly strong combatant, and a great leader. After Rick begins taking her on more adventures and giving her a chance to prove herself, Summer is able to gain Rick's respect until he comes to view her asThe Reliable One. Even Morty seems aware that Summer is essentially this compared to him, as several episodes have him readily acknowledging that Summer is more intelligent than him or have him mention her excellent leadership. Achievements in Ignorance: In "Childrick of Mort," when Rick finds himself in aCurb-Stomp Battlewith Reggie, Summer and Morty accidentally save Rick's life by crashing a spaceship into the back of Reggie's head, killing him instantly. Rick outright admits that this single act makes both Morty and Summer his "heroes." A-Cup Angst: The Rushed Licensed Adventure game reveals that she wears double D bras despite her size being much smaller, claiming she'll grow into them because "Mom's got big boobs."Turns up in the show properi

characters.name: Space Beth
characters.description: A version of Beth who seemingly took Rick's offer in"The ABC's of Beth"to leave her family behind to travel the cosmos on her own. Despite being called "Clone Beth" byPocket Mortys, it's never revealed whether she's a clone or the original Beth, with behind-the-scenes material calling her "Space Beth". Action Girl: While Beth was always badass, she usually reserved displaying it for emergencies only. Space Beth spends much of her new life fighting and has upgraded herself accordingly. Ambiguous Clone Ending:Invoked. Rick continuously flip-flops on whether she or Earth Beth is the clone, repeatedly claiming to both that they're the real one and the other is the fake. When he watches the Mind Blower at the end, it reveals that Rick randomly swapped the two around and looked away to make sure he himself wouldn't know which is which. The promotion forPocket Mortysnames her as "Clone Beth" but nobody in the show knows or cares about who is the real Beth. By Season 5, everyone just calls her "Space Beth". Amicable Exes: Since this version of Beth never reconciled with Jerry, as she left her whole family behind to go on space adventures, she is this with him (despite Jerry expressing happiness that he now has "two wives", since it's pretty clear that this Beth doesn't want to get back with him). She is incredulous that Earth Beth decided to take him back and mocks their relationship once or twice, but when Rick points out that Earth Beth is indeed the same person like her and still decided to get back together with Jerry, Space Beth has no response, implying that she still has unresolved feelings for him of some kind.She also, despite considering herself divorced from Jerry, still keeps her married name. After Jerry manages to distract Phoenix Person long enough for Space Beth to deactivate him, she admits with a smile that he "has his moments", and at least doesn't seem to mind being in his presence.Zig-Zagged by "Bethic Twinstinct", it's implied that she joins Earth Beth

characters.name: Diane Sanchez
characters.description: The wife of Rick Sanchez and mother to Beth. Very little is known about her other than the fact Rick abandoned her and their daughter sometime before his twenty-two-year-long disappearance. The Season 5 premiere confirmed that her name was Diane. Awful Wedded Life:Subverteddepending of which version you are talking about. The version of Diane who was Morty's grandmother was married to Rick Prime who legit abandoned his family for selfish reasons. Meanwhile, the version of Rick the series follows wasHappily Marriedto his version of Diane. Cessation of Existence:Rick Prime reveals that due to the Omega Device, which he put a version of Diane through, all multiversal variants of her no longer exist. This effect goes as far as beyond the reaches of the Central Finite Curve and the memories of anyone in the multiverse who knew Diane.All just so Rick C-137 won’teverget his wife back in any capacity again. The only Diane left in all of reality is not really her at all but a sentient memory of her. Deader than Dead:Not only is Rick's Diane gone, butevery single version of heracross the multiverse has been erased from existence. Even other people’s memories of her (except for one) have all been erased, so there is literally no trace left of her within the universe. Death by Origin Story: Invoked by Rick when he uses a fabricated memory of her and a child Beth's deaths which supposedly led to his current lifestyle.Turned out it was true after all. And then Rick Prime went one step further and used the Omega Device to ensure this occurred witheverypossible iteration of Diane across the Multiverse, further denying Main Rick the chance to reunite with even a vestige of his love out of epic petty spite.

characters.name: Joyce and Leonard Smith
characters.description: Jerry's mother and father. Casual Kink: Joyce likes to make out with Jacob while Leonard watches from a closet dressed as Superman. They're also close enough to Jacob that they bring him along to family gatherings. Only Jerry seems to think this is weird. Good Parents: They're both very loving and supportive of Jerry. Even Rick is nice to them, or at least nicer than he is to Jerry. Happily Married: 40 years and going on strong. Jacob was only brought in to experience something new before one of them passed away. Uncertain Doom: Exactly what happened to them in the original universe after everyone in the world was Cronenberged is never stated (since they're also Morty's grandparents and like Rick are thus immune to the virus). Same for the second Universe as Mr. Frundles essentially became the planet in season 6.

characters.name: Morty Jr.
characters.description: The result of Morty spending a lot of time with a Gazorpazorpian breeding chamber, which is more of a Fembot, Morty Jr. is a half-human, half-Gazorpazorpian creature that Morty takes the responsibility of raising. Always Chaotic Evil: Parodied. As a Gazorpazorpian, all Morty Jr. wants to do is destroy and dominate. The biggest joke in the episode is that despite Morty's best efforts (which aren't very good) he can't override that base programming. Baby's First Words: The first sign of his Gazorpazorpian instincts.Morty Jr.:Da!Morty:Oh, what was that Morty Jr.?! We-were you gonna say 'da-da'? Say da-da!Morty Jr.:DEATH!Morty:(concerned) ...Da-da.Morty Jr.:DOMINATION! Ambiguous Situation: Given that Morty (with some help from Brad Anderson) was able to convince Morty Jr. to not be outwardly violent, it's unclear if this was possible simply due to him being half-human, or if it was due to his environment. The male Gazorpians we see are savages, and Morty Jr. does have some clear inherently destructive urges, but the savage society we see is largely due to the fact that they are literally launched into a barren wasteland from birth, leaving it unclear if Morty's intervention is what helped Morty Jr., or if he could overcome it thanks to having more human-like genes. Bad Is Good and Good Is Bad: Basically what his morality consists of, at least growing up. He doesn’t care about love like Morty tries to teach him, but instead thinks death, destruction and domination of the enemy is more important. He does genuinely care about Morty and decides to channel his inherent bloodthirst into writing instead.

characters.name: Morty's Original Family
characters.description: The Smith family from Morty's home dimension. Following the events of"Rick Potion #9"where Rick and Morty's actions cause the apocalypse, the pair move to a new dimension, abandoning Morty's original Jerry, Beth and Summer as the last human beings on an earth overrun with killer mutants. For more on Jerry in particular, see his entry inRick and Morty: Variants. Asshole Victim: Deconstructed.While they were Morty's family, Beth was very quick to disown Morty and Rick (something Jerry and Summer were very quick to agree too). When Morty returned with an alternate Summer to show her the aftermath of Rick's adventures, Jerry destroyed the portal gun in order to force Morty to be with them and nearly killed Summer until they were frozen by the Citadel (which inadvertently caused the deaths of Beth and Summer when they neglected to thaw them out). With Jerry as the last human on Earth, he reminds Morty that he, Beth, and Summer were still people at the end of the day and didn't deserve to be tossed aside so callously because of what both Rick and Morty did. Back for the Dead:Summer and Beth died sometime after the Season 3 premiere. Jerry appears in the premiere for Season 6, only to be killed off inThe Stingerby Rick Prime. Badass Family: A father, a mother and a daughter. All badass Cronenburg killers. Battle Couple: Jerry and Beth form one in "Rick Potion #9", fighting Cronenburgs together.

characters.name: Paul Fleishman
characters.description: Beth's husband in multiple dimensions where she remarries. Hasn't appeared in any "main" dimension yet. Hopeless with Tech: His skills with technology is on par or below that of the average Jerry, reaching out to Season 2 Jerry for some help with the TV at the Jerryboree. Nice Guy: Based on the version of him from the Jerryboree, he's a caring man who loves Beth very much and supports his Morty without trying to replace his world's Jerry.

characters.name: GoTronFamilies
characters.description: Four variants of the family that Rick teams up with to collect everyGoTronferret across the multiverse. The only variants who don't look perfectly alike are the Ricks. Alliance of Alternates: Rick forms one with alternate Ricks and their families to combine theirGoTroncollections and make even biggerGoTronMechs. The end result ends up strongly resembling a mafia crime family, especially with Rick's alternate selves having personality and appearance quirks that wouldn't be too out of place in such a setting. Averted with Morty, who feels alienated from his alternate counterparts because they've all gone to Boobworld and he hasn't. Combining Mecha: Taken up a notch when the alternate Smith Families gather their ownGoTronsto form their ownGoTronMechs, so Rick can modify them to fuse into an evenlarger"GoGoTron". At the climax of the episode, Rick Sanchez' operation was able to acquire enoughGoTronsto fusethoseGoGoTronsinto a single ridiculously largeGoGoGoTron. Humongous Mecha: The titularGoTronFerrets, which are five multi-colored ferret-shaped mechs that can combine into a single humanoidGoTronmech. Summer and Rick form acrime family-styleoperation with other Ricks to complete their ownGoTroncollections so Rick-C137 can modify theirGoTronsto combine to form an even largerGoGoTron(made up of 25 of the smallerGoTronFerrets). Near the climax, Rick has made fiveGoGoTronmechs and modified them to form a super-massiveGoGoGoTron(125GoTronferrets), with the resulting cockpits being the size of a hotel lobby. Even with all that size, the resultingGoGoGoTronmech is barely larger than Naruto Smith's arm. Mecha Expansion Pack: As part of "The Family" business, Rick utilizes the ferrets of other realities to combine fiveGoTronsinto an even largerGoGoTron, and then combine five ofthoseGoGoTronsinto the massiveGoGoGoTron.

characters.name: Jerry’s Original Family
characters.description: The family from Dimension 5126 that Jerry used to belong to before winding up with his current family due to a mix up at the Jerryboree. Dysfunctional Family: This family is constantly at each other's throats the same way the main family used to be in season 2, insulting and belittling each other at every chance. While their main counterparts still have plenty of issues, the dynamic shown here proves things could be far worse. I Have No Son!: Our Jerry has no problem leaving this family behind once the family he's been living with since season 2 comes to get him. Kick the Dog: They relentlessly mock Jerry in the same way they used to in the first two seasons, who hasn't seen them since "Mortynight Run" and simply sits there watching them bicker. When his current family comes to pick him up,he rightfully flips them offand rejoins the main versions. Point of Divergence: Due to not spending any time separated from each other like the Jerry and Beth we've been following, Beth is a lot more hostile towards everyone especially Jerry who she refers to as a "living receptacle of human fear". Season 2 Jerry isn't much better in that front. And Morty got expelled, which our Morty has managed to avoid.

characters.name: Mooch Jerry's Family
characters.description: The Smith-Sanchez family from Mooch Jerry's home dimension. Anger Born of Worry: Mooch's original family is understandably upset that he disappeared on them, particularly because even though they're often short-tempered or oblivious to him, it doesn't mean that they hate him. In Spite of a Nail: As can be seen in the above image, even this family had their own Snuffles. Girls With Mustaches: Beth and Summer have 5 o'clock shadows. It can be assumed that this is the case for everyone on their Earth, regardless of gender. Perma-Stubble: They've all got a 5 o'clock shadow despite Rick, Paul, and possibly Morty being the only ones who could realisitically grow that amount of facial hair.

characters.name: Hostage Family
characters.description: A cooperative version of the family (sans Morty) that Evil Morty is holding hostage just above the Omega Device, so if Rick doesn't cooperate with him, every Rick, Beth, Jerry and Summer in the multiverse pays the price. Generic Cuteness: They all have identical faces in a cloyingly saccharine style. The Needless: They're content to just sit on a couch for the rest of their lives, they don't even need to go to the bathroom. What Happened to the Mouse?: After the Omega Device is destroyed, the hostage Smiths that were inside aren't seen or mentioned again, leaving it unclear what happened to them.

characters.name: Good Family
characters.description: A seemingly well-adjusted version of the family that recently lost their son, and cut ties with their Rick long ago. All There in the Manual: The captions call them the "Good" Smiths. The only other designation is that they call their Morty Mort. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome:Played With. They are ostensibly a happier, more well-adjusted Smith family who refuse to tolerate Rick's antics (which resulted in him becoming a professor, with a new wife, and becoming sober) and clearly express their love for their son. However, their Jerry was aControl Freakwho pushed Morty into extreme athletics to "make him strong", which ended up killing him. However, it’s possible they would have grieved normally and moved on eventually; it's only because ofMorty's influencethat they were corrupted and eventuallywiped out. Ambiguously Evil: While Good Jerry is revealed to actually be a controlling, domineering father who pushed his son into extreme activities against his will that eventually killed him, it's unclear if Good Beth and Summer were aware of this, and if their joining Jerry is due to complicity or sheer grief. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Good Jerry seems like a better father than the main Jerry, being a caring, attentive father to his Mort. But then reveals himself to be a highly controlling, obsessive freak who pushed his son into extreme activities against his will that led to his death. And then forces Morty to stay with him and become his new son instead, resorting to violence and murder when crossed.

characters.name: Other Smith-Sanchez Families
characters.description: Variants of the Smith-Sanchez family that Jerry and Mooch Jerry encounter on their interdimensional travels. Advertised Extra: Goat Beth and Picasso Summer appear in the Season 8 promotional image, but are limited to a brief scene in this episode. Apocalypse How: Mooch and Jerry pass through a universe that has completely frozen over, and another where Rick turned the moon into a giant disco ball that reflects deadly beams of sunlight across the surface of the Earth. The Grand Central dimension is also implied to have suffered some sort of catastrophe, as nothing but Jerries and one Rick live there. Black Comedy: In a dimension where people are toast, funerals aren't quite so solemn due to their recently buried springing out of the ground. Blah, Blah, Blah: In one dimension everyone communicates by saying "blah" over and over.

characters.name: Decoy Families
characters.description: The decoys are fake members of the Smith family made by Rick to hide from his enemies. Most if not all of the decoys have also made decoys. Androids Are People, Too: It is mentioned numerous times that the decoys are still sentient beings, even the incredibly poorly made straw-Rick is fully sentient. Bait-and-Switch:The family in the beginning appears to be the real Smiths, only to be killed off by squid aliens and another Rick to get an alert saying a decoy family was killed, implying they're the real Smiths. Then, after the opening credits,they'rekilled off, switching to another Rick with his family, getting another alert, and so on.Muppet-Rickis actually Rick disguised as a decoy that's too obvious and too adorable to kill. He's still a decoy though.We're first led to believe this episode will be about the Smiths being hunted by Squid aliens, then it turns out the squids are just more decoys who became self-aware and started killing off the other decoys. The family in the beginning appears to be the real Smiths, only to be killed off by squid aliens and another Rick to get an alert saying a decoy family was killed, implying they're the real Smiths. Then, after the opening credits,they'rekilled off, switching to another Rick with his family, getting another alert, and so on. Muppet-Rickis actually Rick disguised as a decoy that's too obvious and too adorable to kill. He's still a decoy though.

characters.name: Night Family
characters.description: Alternate selves for the Smith family that take over their unconscious bodies while their main selves are asleep, thanks to a device called the Somnamulator. Anti-Villain: While they no doubt want to make their day counterparts pay for their oppression, their goals are still understandable given what they endure before this. They're even willing to enact a truce after escalated aggression into outright war and go back to way things were, but Rick proves too obstinate. Bedtime Brainwashing: Their existence is due to a machine called the Somnambulator mind controlling their day selves as they sleep. Driven to Suicide: After they go broke due to their unsustainably expensive lifestyle, they surrender themselves to their day counterparts by destroying the Somnambulator. Enemy Within: Grow into this as time goes by and become threats to their day selves wellbeing everytime they go to sleep. Night Summer in particular claims to have always existed within Summer's subconscious, unleashed by the Somnambulator.

characters.name: Rick and MortyC-131
characters.description: The native Rick and Morty of Dimension C-131 (Replacement Dimension). After fixing the Cronenberg Crisis, they both end up dying in aFreak Lab Accident. The Main Rick and Morty then arrive and take their places in the new dimension. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Rick C-131 manages to cure the Cronenberg epidemic, whereas Rick C-137 failed to do so. Freak Lab Accident: Both Rick and Morty C-131 met their untimely deaths when the Ionic Defibulizer exploded after Rick C-131 finished it. Point of Divergence: Rick C-131 lived a life very similar to Rick C-137 up until the Cronenberg epidemic, but manages to cure it before his and his grandson's untimely death by finishing the Ionic Defibulizer. Too Happy to Live: Both Rick and Morty C-131 seem to have a better disposition than Rick C-137 and Morty Prime, especially after fixing the Cronenberg epidemic. Though they ended up being killed in aFreak Lab Accidentupon C-131 Rick finishing his Ionic Defibulizer.

characters.name: Evil Rick
characters.description: A sarcastic clapping, serial killer alternate version of Rick. In reality, he is a robotic puppet being controlled by Evil Morty. Actually a Doombot: He was set up as theBig Badof his first appearance, but turned out to just be a cyborg that the real villain was controlling through his eyepatch. Body Horror: After Evil Rick's death, a piece of his headcomes off to reveal sparking wires. One of the investigating Ricks cuts open his skull to reveal that his brain is more wires and circuits than flesh, which outs Evil Rick asmerely a puppet under someone else's control. Create Your Own Villain: His constant abuse towards his Morty eventually led to him becoming Evil Morty, turning Evil Rick into his own puppet and starting his quest to escape the Central Finite Curve while killing any version of Rick and Morty necessary. Death Seeker: After much suffering under Evil Mortys control, he tries repeatedly to take his own lifebut is prevented from doing so. After the captured Mortys escape and rebel, Evil Rick does nothing to stop them and even urges them to kill him.

characters.name: Fascist Ricks and Fascist Morty
characters.description: A series of alternate-dimension Ricks (and a Morty) that all support a fascist regime and never cancelled Project Phoenix, allowing Rick C-137 to be cloned into their dimensions, much to his regret. Affably Evil: Shrimp Rick establishes himself as one of the most polite and compassionate Ricks as he was concerned for Rick C-137's health when he came out of the cloning facility and had a very cordial conversation with C-137 about the similarities and differences of their cultures. It's only when C-137 reveals that he isn't a fascist that Shrimp Rick turns on him, and even then he doesn't personally kill him despite having the means to do so. Alternate-History Nazi Victory: Rick'sBody Backup Drivethat he never properly decommissioned past destroying his own backups keeps uploading him into parallel universes run by fascists. Thoroughly lampshaded by Rick, who quickly grows exasperated enough to immediately kill himself and pop to the next universe at the first sign of fascism. Bears Are Bad News: One of these Fascist Ricks is a blue-furred teddy bear. In Spite of a Nail: It's commented on that, even though his universe is run by shrimp instead of humans, Shrimp Rick's Earth is uncannily identical to realities run by humans.

characters.name: Wasp Rick
characters.description: Wasp Rick is a surprisingly kind alternate-dimension Rick,despite being a wasp. Facial Horror: Wasp Rick explains that he can lay eggs into the eyes of his prey, which then eat their way out.He does this exact thing to Hologram Rick. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He's about as unpleasant as Ricks tend to be but he's shown to be quite warm to his family. It's actually anInvoked Tropeon his end. As he explains it, the life of a wasp is so inherently horrific that having a bit of empathy isn't the worst way of doing things. Parasites Are Evil: Played with; a parasitoid wasp, Wasp Rick makes it abundantly clear that their way of life involves eating their prey alive and laying their eggs in their eyeballs... and yet, he's easily one of the nicer Ricks in the multiverse, with a much healthier relationship with his family and happier home life in general. Pet the Dog: He ends up helping Rick C-137 get back to his dimension and to his body without much fuss. He even saves Rick C-137 and Mortyfrom a gigantic Hologram Rick.

characters.name: RickC-132
characters.description: A Rick not too far removed from Rick C-137. This live action Rick has jumped to another dimension with his Morty, in search of a new home.Officially named Rick C-132 by Adult Swim with the teaser of a live-action episode. Casting Gag:Rick and Mortybegan life as a raunchy parody ofBack to the Future, with Rick being a parody of Doc Brown. Christopher Lloyd playing this Rick brings the joke full circle. Old Shame: RickC-132is pretty miffed MortyC-132thought he would turn himself into a pickle again, stating "Are you kidding?(spits out piece of pickle)NEVER!"

characters.name: Space Jam Rick and Morty
characters.description: They are variants of Rick & Morty who cameoed in theSpace Jamsequel. Actually a Doombot: Created specifically to assure fans the much reviledSpace Jamcameo wasn't the real Rick and Mortyand to be killed off. Adaptational Dumbass: Rick calls the Tasmanian Devil a "badger thing" and admits he can't treat Taz's insanity. Death by Cameo: Their one canonical appearance in the show is as corpses in body bags after Rick kills them. Death Seeker: When Rick C-137 came to their dimension, they begged him to kill them.

characters.name: Addict Rick
characters.description: The Rick from Boss Jerry's dimension. Unlike most Ricks, this one was dominated by his Jerry into being a hapless slave. Ambiguous Situation: Did this Rick come from beyond the Central Finite Curve? He's weak enough to be subordinate to a Jerry (albeit a particularly aggressive Jerry), but he's intelligent enough to have already developed portal technology. The Dog Bites Back: Subverted. Addict Rick tries to stand up to Boss Jerry after being bullied for too long, complaining about how he doesn't like getting pulled out of his chair. Boss Jerry just shoves him back in his place. Grew a Spine: Subverted. Addict Rick starts to stand up for himself when Boss Jerry forces him out of his chair, but he's too addled to keep it up and Boss Jerry browbeats him back into submission. Shadow Archetype: Most Ricks are hedonistic, but this Rick lost all self-control, leaving him anEmpty Shellto be abused by a Jerry.

characters.name: Sunglasses Morty
characters.description: A Morty that shows up at multiversal yard sales to scavenge from his dead counterparts, and has a habit of attending the funerals of other Mortys. Attending Your Own Funeral: He has a portal gun of his own, and uses it to attend the funerals of other Mortys. Eye Scream: Those sunglasses are actually his real eyes. He can't take them off, only tilt them to reveal red connective tissue underneath. Forced Transformation: Blaming his latest trauma on this variant, Morty Prime zaps him with a raygun that turns Sunglasses Morty into a dog with an overly-long neck. His Rick proceeds to gleefully zap himself with that raygun.

characters.name: Sober Rick
characters.description: A Rick that was ousted by his daughter's husband and forced to address his alcoholism. He lives in sobriety, has managed to become a respected and liked college professor and has a new wife: Uli. The Alcoholic: The only Rick to address his addictions, though he eventually falls off the wagon as the stress of building a functioning portal gun gets to him. All for Nothing: Due to Morty pushing him to develop interdimensional travel so he could get back home, Professor Rick ends up becoming obsessed with it at the cost of ruining his job and marriage. And to top it off, his portal invention didn't even work, creating portals that kill anything that goes through it. And then he and his family get killed in a shoot-out. The Corruptible: He seems more put-together than other versions of Rick at first, but his desperate drive to complete the portal gun—with Morty's prodding—drove him back into his characteristic self-destructive tendencies, ruining seventeen years of sobriety in a few days. Cool Teacher: This version of Rick is a popular mathematics professor at MIT.

characters.name: Tiny Rick
characters.description: A younger clone of Rick with Rick's consciousness in it. The Ace: He quickly becomes the most popular kid at school. Morty also notes that he is an extremely good wingman, having managed to set up a date between him and Jessica. Alternate Self: Tiny Rick is just Rick in a teenage body, but the change in hormones and brain chemistry changes Rick's normal outlook and behavior in a similar manner to psychological drugs. The way Tiny Rick is always positive and upbeat is more than a little similar to the effects of someone taking an anti-depressant. Body Backup Drive: Tiny Rick was a part of what Rick had dubbed "Operation Phoenix", a series of clones of himself at different growth states he could transfer his consciousness to in the event he died. The wholeunfortunate business that happened withTiny Rick,however, leads Rick to conclude that the project was a mistake, so he destroys all the clones with an axe. Despair Event Horizon: Summer and Morty uses depressing music to invoke this in him, combining it with his innate teenage angst and makes him want to return to cynical old age.

characters.name: Healthy Rick and Healthy Morty
characters.description: The positive sides of Rick and Morty's personalities, at least from their perspectives. Healthy Rick is a meek and politeCool Old Guythat feels a sense of responsibility towards his large knowledge and Healthy Morty is an upbeat popular kid who never loses self-confidence. The Ace: Not long before he came around, Healthy Morty gets seeminglyeveryonein the school to love him and helps with their homework (including math and music). He moves on to become a successful stockbroker with a hot, red-headed girlfriend. Ambiguous Situation: At the end of the episode, Healthy Morty does not end the call that he suspects Rick is using to track him down. Whether it was his own decision to get his toxins back, a subconscious decision or an accident is anyone's guess. The DVD commentary confirmed that Morty unconsciously left his phone on. Cannot Tell a Lie: And they're healthy enough to admit that. Extreme Doormat: Downplayed with Healthy Rick. He wasn't okay with getting trapped in the toxic dimension andwillfight if he has to. But he was briefly willing to let Toxic Rick turn the whole world toxic.

characters.name: Toxic Rick and Toxic Morty
characters.description: The negative sides of Rick's and Morty's personalities, at least from their perspectives. Anthropomorphic Personification: They're the embodiments of everything Rick and Morty seem to find negative and or wrong about themselves. This includes Rick's attachment to Morty (which he views as irrational) and Morty'sempathy. Assimilation Plot: Toxic Rick decides to toxify the whole world using a modified detoxification tank. Being Good Sucks: The fact Toxic Morty is the one who has been saddled with Morty's moral compass and ability to feel empathy, seems to at least strongly imply that Morty feels weighed down by his nice nature and a strong sense of justice. Chemistry Can Do Anything: In the detoxification tank, where everything is made of a nebulous toxin counterpart to conventional elements, Toxic Rick discovers a new form of electricity and constructs a device that allows him to escape after contacting Rick.

characters.name: Hologram Rick
characters.description: A holographic AI Rick installed into Morty to make sure Rick is cloned back whenever he's killed. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Despite claiming that's a harmful AI stereotype, he turns evil when he becomes solid. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: Becomes giant when he gains solid form. Eye Scream:He is killed when Wasp Rick lays his eggs in his eye, with the larva eating their way out moments later. A God Am I: Upon being turned into a solid giant by the ferrofluid, he immediately declares "I'm a fucking god! You're fucked!".

characters.name: Memory Rick
characters.description: Memory Rick is a younger, more idealistic version of Rick, constructed from Birdperson's memories of Rick at that age. He became a sentient memory after meeting the real Rick and later followed him to aid Rick in his goal of reviving their friend Birdperson. Actually Pretty Funny: He admits that Rick throwing a bucket over his head and trapping him in a shipping container was “charmingly analogue.” Alternate Self: He is a version of a younger Rick formed from Birdperson's memories. From Rick's attitude, however, it seems that it's an accurate recollection. And I Must Scream: He gets trappedin Jerry's head after they formJerRicky. Because Jerry is incapable of understanding technology beyond "springs and gears" any technology he tries to make to escape turns into springs and gears. The Anti-Nihilist: He takes this attitude on being a memory of Rick rather than his own person, due to Rick himself already having a similar attitude from his experiences traveling the multiverse. He initially views the real Rick as aStraw Nihilistdue to letting his cynicism about it get to him.

characters.name: Adult Morty
characters.description: After Morty artificially aged himself into a 40-year-old, Rick took him to the Citadel to subtract the excess age, which forms into a 26-year-old version of Morty. Fanservice Pack: Adult Morty is quite handsome. It's implied that this is because he's technically a newborn who hasn't been loaded with the baggage that comes from being Rick's sidekick, while the source-Morty could just as easily get worse-looking with age. We Hardly Knew Ye: He's shot to death by some police Mortys mere seconds after being brought into existence. Wide-Eyed Idealist: By his own admission he's not quite ready to sell out and wants to be a famous influencer. Younger Than They Look: He's only a few seconds old, but resembles a hypothetical version of Morty as an adult.

characters.name: Marta
characters.description: Informed Judaism: Her and her family are meant to be Jewish. However, because Morty knows very little about Judaism, it becomes more of a informed trait. Soul Fragment: She is one of billions of fragments of Morty's personality in the game.

characters.name: Rick Bot
characters.description: A "new, nicer Rick" robot made by Rick to take his place with the family. Actually a Doombot: We don't find out he's not the real Rick until his second appearance. Almost Dead Guy: Rickbot is sliced open by five tiny lightsabers, but hangs on long enough for some dying words. Rick even complains about how long it's taking him to actually die. Bait-and-Switch: We were originally led to believe this was the real Rick pretending to be nice andoverly supportiveas one of his elaborate revenge plans against Morty for talking back to him and going against him commands, turns out it was a robot replica designed to be niceand was a little too good at it. Death Seeker: Once Rickbot isrevealed to be a robotand Morty is infuriated by the deception, the former becomes increasingly guilty about lying to everyone, especially as the rest of the Smiths shower him with more and moreOblivious Guilt Slinging. By the time all three Smith women attack him after Morty tells them the truth, he gladly welcomes death, and is outright disappointed when they revive him to help save the Earth, repeatedly attempting to commitHeroic Sacrificesand otherwise put himselfIn Harm's Wayso he can end it. He finally gets his wish near the end after taking five mini-lightsabers from a gatling gun to the stomach.

characters.name: Matrix Morty
characters.description: A version of Morty that, along with Summer, is forced to grow up in a simulated world thathates borrowing phone chargers without permissionwhen Rick falls asleep after trapping them both inside. He isnothappy about it when they both break free. Fanservice Pack: Much like the version of him seen in "Rickmurai Jack", he has grown into quite a handsome, fit young man, this time as a result of surviving prison, joining the Matrix's fire brigade, and later enlisting as a soldier, making him ripped. The Hermit: He wentOff the Gridafter Summer's war for lithium, residing in a cabin in the woods with onlytwo dogsfor companionship. Rage Breaking Point: If surviving nearly two decades in Rick's Matrix wasn't enough to drive him insane, watching Rick casually allow Beth to take his phone charger,which was the reason he and Summer were trapped there in the first place,definitelywas. Resurrective Immortality: Rick's Matrix prevented him and Summer from dying while inside, which ended up making Morty useful to Summer in her war effort.

characters.name: Ted
characters.description: An amnesiac alter ego Rick takes on whenever he wants to take a vacation from being himself. Amnesiac Dissonance: Bereft of Rick's memories, Ted is a humble, simple man who is open with his friends and loved ones. Amnesiac Resonance: He is still as smart and capable as Rick, he just needed the motivation. Tragically, the events of the episode has him effectively turn into Rick even before he restores his memories. Body Horror: Rick's extensive cybernetic modifications are triggered by the slightest agitation, which horrifies Ted when he finds out his body has been tampered with at a point in time he can't remember. Everyone Has Standards: Travels 400 light years with his friends to goRamboon Rick, but refuses to hurt the Smith-Sanchez family, seeing them as innocent (despite recognizing Morty as the voice telling him to go back to being Rick).

characters.name: Rick's Head
characters.description: Eye Beams: Rick's head is initially helpless, but Morty brings him to an electronics store where he's able to swallow enough technology and integrate into himself to give himself laser eyes. Literal Split Personality: Rick having his head split from his body also splits their personality traits. The head is unconstrained by Rick's various physical ailments and behaves much more thoughtfully. The Needless: Rick not having his body naturally means not having any of his body's needs, but this also means not having his body's want like his addiction to alcohol. Being sober without any urges that would compromise his rationality is of the many perks that makes him reconsider getting his body back. Never My Fault: Rick tricks Morty into signing consent forms to have his head transplanted onto Morty's body. The doctor obviously doesn't go along with this without first checking if Morty is aware of what he consented to, and Rick grumbles that he's being a nosy meddler. Oracular Head: Thanks to airbag implants in his neck, Rick can survive decapitation and even talk for a while, though he has to build himself a replacement body before the airbags completely deflate.

characters.name: Rick's Body
characters.description: Cooldown Hug: Rick's body hugs the leader of the thieves rather than continue to attack him, which causes the leader to realize his mistake and leave peacefully. Summer is incredulous that a mere hug could accomplish such a thing, but changes her mind when Rick's body hugs her. Disability Immunity: Rick's head attempts aSuper-Screamon his body, but it fails because the device that allows his body to perceive the world is just a piece of technology that doesn't actually suffer any harm from said noise where an actual, organic head would. In Case of X, Break Glass: Rick's body has a tiny emergency lever behind glass with a tiny hammer to break said glass, which serves to activate his most dangerous implants once pulled. Literal Split Personality: Rick having his head split from his body also splits their personality traits. The body is "all heart" and is considerably nicer than Rick is. That being said, Rick’s body is also saddled with his various vices like lust, and he ruins Rick’s friendship with ahot alien mechanic womanafter sleeping with her and making things awkward. Screw Yourself: Though Rick denies it afterwards, it’s heavily implied the head and body’s solution to reconcile their differences was for the former to give the latter a blowjob.

characters.name: Alternate Reality Beth
characters.description: Beth from a dimension where Jerry never got her pregnant, going on to become a surgeon for humans. The Alcoholic: This Beth drinks even more frequently than the main Beth. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Comparatively. This Beth is a surgeon for people instead of horses. Artistic License – Animal Care: Alternate reality Beth keeps large parrots like macaws and cockatoos in old-fashioned bird cages that are too small for even a parakeet, let alone large birds. It's a Wonderful Plot: Played around with. This Beth is a human surgeon but is sad and alone.

characters.name: Mytholog Beths
characters.description: Living visualizations of how Jerry views Beth. Can't Kill You, Still Need You: The Beth Mytholog doesn't hurt the original Beth because she needs her mind to create more Worm Jerrys with the perception device. She does strap Beth into a chair with a metal bar, to ensure that she doesn't get any ideas. Demonization: Part of the point of the alien couples counselling. They use a machine to bring to life a spouse's worst perception of their partner as part of the therapy. From Jerry's perspective, Beth is portrayed as a vicious, egotistical monster. It's only when the machine is hooked up to a Jerry mytholog that loves Beth unconditionally that a wholly benevolent Beth is formed. Deity of Human Origin: The goddess version of Beth is basically this, being an all-powerfulDeus ex Machinaformed from a human template. Deus ex Machina: A literal example. Jerry resolves the conflict with the monster Beth by using the perception machine on an idealized version of Jerry. This improved Jerry's perception of Beth conjures agoddess version of herthat immediately obliterates the monster version.

characters.name: Memory Beths
characters.description: Alliance of Alternates: After Memory Diane accidentally wakes up a memory of Beth by telling her she is a memory, Memory Beth assembles every single memory of herself who gang up on Memory Rick and Memory Diane to flush the intruders out of her brain. Enfant Terrible: There are three child Beths in their midst, two of them froma recent memory of de-aging with Space Beth. What the Hell, Hero?: When they have him in their grasps, they rightfully blame Memory Rick for driving the real Beth insane, to the point she’s about to commit suicide due to all the conflicting memories in her head, just because he wanted to save the last fragment of Rick’s memory of Diane.

characters.name: Alternate Reality Jerry
characters.description: Jerry from a dimension where he never got Beth pregnant, going on to become a successful (but severely untalented) filmmaker. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Subverted. While this Jerry may have attained fame and fortune, it clearly wasn't through any merit. The trappings of fame eventually overwhelm Jerry and he has a breakdown, finding Alternate Beth and telling her he loves her. Creator Breakdown: In-universe, this Jerry suffers one after writing and directingWeekend at Dead Cat Lady's House II. It's a Wonderful Plot: Played around with. If Jerry never got Beth pregnant he would have made it big in Hollywood, but at the same time he's still unhappy because he doesn't have Beth in his life. Low-Speed Chase: Alternate Jerry leads the cops on a slow-speedHot Pursuitin a lawnmower.

characters.name: Jerryboree Jerrys
characters.description: Identical Twin ID Tag: Certain Jerrys who have more than background roles will have identifying features to make them distinct from the main Jerry. Manchild: They get handled quite easily like naive children by the staff, including one wearing a very obviously fake Beth costume. Me's a Crowd: Many Jerrys reside and hang out here together, though not by choice since none of them have any means of going home.

characters.name: Mytholog Jerrys
characters.description: A living visualization of how Beth views Jerry. Action Hero: The muscular Jerrys wield machine guns and don't wear shirts, mimicking 80's action heroes. Alliance of Alternates: An army of heroic and vain Jerrys who take on an army of worm Jerrys. Clone Army: The Beth Mytholog starts to create an army of Worm Jerries toTake Over the World. Feather Boa Constrictor: The worm-like Jerry Mytholog briefly takes on this role for the Beth Mytholog.

characters.name: Wooden Jerry
characters.description: One of the examples of the lazier decoys made by another decoy of Rick Sanchez. This one, like the rest of his decoy family, is completely made of wood. His only goal is to use a can of varnish to cross the river. Ambiguous Situation: It's unclear if he's immortal because he's a wooden automaton or because he used an entire can of varnish to coat himself, though the implications ofThe Stingerlean more towards the latter. And I Must Scream: He's dismembered by beavers and has his torso used as a nest, gets submerged underwater and wakes up in a post-apocalyptic wasteland, has his head mounted on a mirror and then set on fire, then has his head mounted on a cross where an alien version of Jesus is being crucified. The process takes millennia and he's alive for all of it, and none too happy about it either. Apologetic Attacker: After sealing himself away so he'll be safe while his family dies, he tearfully apologizes to them, saying he just wants to live and only has one can of varnish. Although he doesn't seem even mildly upset afterwards. Be Careful What You Wish For: He betrays his family both because he wants to live and because he wants to keep his can of varnish for himself. In the end he gets his varnishandhe gets to live, but his varnish grants him a life of thousands of years of agony that leaves him begging for death.

characters.name: Mooch Jerry
characters.description: A Jerry that explores the Multiverse, encouraging the main Jerry to go on adventures with him. Dirty Coward: As it turns out, Mooch chose to live the life of a dimension-traveling nomad because he left his family and was too scared to reconcile with them after being away for so long. Jerry's quick to call him out on this and forces him to confront his family. Dissatisfied Family Man: He postures at being free and independent, but after a number of misadventures land them in Mooch's home dimension, Jerry discovers that Mooch was married and walked out on his family out of boredom with his life. Foreshadowing: The way Mooch frantically tries to finish his cereal while running away from Jerry hints that he's reliant on others for basic resources. Perma-Stubble: To make him distinct from the main Jerry, this Jerry has a five o'clock shadow. When returned to his native dimension, we see this applies to the entire human race, as Beth, Morty, Summer, Rick and Beth's new husband have the same facial hair.

characters.name: Boss Jerry
characters.description: A Jerry that started a crime gang of Jerrys to exploit multiversal travel. Alliance of Alternates: Boss Jerry collects Jerries whose families have gone into space and never came back. They wear red headbands and live in a rundown version of the house with an addict Rick. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: Boss Jerry is at least competent enough to have browbeaten a Rick into servitude, though clearly not one remotely as self-confident as Rick C-137, and formed his own protection racket like a poor man's Citadel. Beard of Evil: He's got a full beard to make him look more menacing than Jerry or Mooch Jerry. The Dog Bites Back: This Jerry successfully dominated his Rick, leaving him anEmpty Shell.

characters.name: Matrix Summer
characters.description: A version of Summer that, along with Morty, is forced to grow up in a simulated world thathates borrowing phone chargers without permissionwhen Rick falls asleep after trapping them both inside. She eventually manages to get them both free using...Questionable methods. Corrupt Corporate Executive:Invoked. She figured out the only way to escape Rick's Matrix without him is by exploiting itsobsession with phone chargers, so she spends years taking over and monopolizing its tech industry, which not only turns her into a multi-billionaire but also the most powerful woman on the planet. Though to Beth's annoyance, she still retains her ruthlessly manipulative personality when she and Morty return to reality. I Did What I Had to Do: After abandoning Morty to rot in a Matrix prison, conquering Rick's matrix, she uses a false-flag attack to start a devastating war on a lithium-rich country, where she secretly uses Morty's immortality in the simulation to win for her. This results in the countless deaths in the Matrix and completely traumatizes Morty, but the lithium she extracts from winning the war allows her to make a device that makes all the Matrix's phones never need charging, creating enough of aLogic Bombto finally free her and Morty from the simulation.

characters.name: Fear Hole Diane
characters.description: A Diane variant that Rick and Morty identify as proof that they're still trapped in the Fear Hole. Birds of a Feather: Her surprising appearance in Fear No Mort shows that she is a lot like Rick in many ways such as pondering Sci-fi concepts, being heavy drinkers, and being willing to accept their deaths for the sake of their loved ones. It is no surprise why Rick loves her very much and was greatly devastated by her loss. Broken Record: When Morty hogs the Hole, Dianeglitches outand repeats the word "true" over and over. A Day in the Limelight: She appears in a vision manifested by the Fear Hole inSeason 7 finalewhere a version of her successfully survives her assassination thanks to her Rick'sHeroic Sacrifice. She spends much of the episode bonding with Rick, who while reluctant comes around to resuming what is implied to be their original dynamic.The episode eventually reveals that Morty was the only one in the hole and while he does have access tosome of Rick's memories, it isunclear how much he actually knows of his grandparents' relationship. Hidden Depths: Assuming her portrayal in "Fear no Mort" is accurate, then Diane was into researching non-human intelligence and even had a Master's degree in the subject. She was also a heavier drinker than her husband was, implying that Rick's present alcoholism may have been taken from her.

characters.name: Memory Diane
characters.description: The vestiges of Diane that Rick extracted from his mind and preserved in artificial grey matter. Color Motif: Yellow and Gold. Aside from her blonde hair, Memory Diane tends to be framed in "golden hour" lighting for full romantic effect. Girls with Guns: She's introduced at a shooting range. Ugly Guy, Hot Wife: Due to Rick's strongest memory of Diane being when he first met her, she's still a vibrant 20-something. Meanwhile Memory Rick is already in his thirties and aging badly, as hisExhausted Eye Bagsdemonstrate.

characters.name: Council of Ricks
characters.description: A large group of Ricks who sought refuge from governmentsby becoming a government.The Rick the show focuses onhas previously refused tobe one of their members. Asshole Victim:There isn't much sympathy for them, after what they can actually do to their grandchildren after Rick sent them off fighting the Galactic Federationat their front doorstep. Became Their Own Antithesis: Rick C-137 describes the Council as this.Rick C-137: I'm the Rick, and so were the rest ofyoubefore you formed this stupid alliance! You wanted to be safe from the government, so you became astupid government! That makes every Rick here less Rick than me! Entertainingly Wrong: While the Council admits their mistake and apologize to C-137 when he proved his innocence in "Close Rick-Counters of the Rick Kind", in retrospect, they were not completely wrong to be initially distrustful when he tries to defend himself when a bunch of Ricks were killed off, as "Rickmurai Jack" reveals thatC-137 did kill dozens, if not hundreds, of Ricks in his initial attempt at finding the Rick responsible for the deaths of his Beth and Diane. Evil Doppelgänger: To Rick C-137, by hiding themselves from the government by becoming the government themselves, enforcing the most atrocious rules to handle their Ricks and their respective grandchildren as their resources. This gives Rick C-137 a good reason to wipe their Council off bywarping the Citadel into the Galactic Federation Prison.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: An organization that governs thousands of planets throughout the universe. Rick and his family have occasionally interacted with its operatives throughout their adventures. In the second season finale, they take over Earth. In Season Three, Rick causes the collapse of the government by completely devaluing their currency. Aerith and Bob: A truly bizarre twist on this. The main "insect people" that seem to be the heads of the Federation follow a naming convention where they all have a very alien-sounding first name, and then a totally mundane last name: Like "Krombopulus Michael" or "Cornvelius Daniel." After the End: Ever since Rick caused their economy to collapse, the Galactic Federation's entire civilization has collapsed into anarchy and madness. Alien Blood: The aliens who run the Federation, the Gromflomites, have dark blue blood. Aliens Are Bastards: The Gromflomites, the primary species of the Galactic Federation, are shown to be highly racist and militaristic and it is heavily implied that they rule the Federation as aMaster Raceand treat all other species as second-class citizens.

characters.name: Rick D. Sanchez III
characters.description: The owner of a wafer factory, as well as the chief spokesman and leader within the Shadow Council in charge of the Citadel. Asshole Victim:He and the Shadow Council get purged by Evil Morty and get unceremoniously tossed into outer space as mere trash; considering that we see him earlier being an utterly evil factory owner who plucked a Rick that chose to live a simple life out of it and then trapped the one Rick that tried to help him to take his place, he more than deserved it. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Considering that he kidnapped Simple Rick for the sake of profit, and is a member of the Shadow Council that made life on The Citadel hell for everyone else, he qualifies as this. Corrupted Character Copy: Literally a Rick version ofWilly Wonka, as he's, in Layman's terms, Willy Wonka if he was a twisted sociopath that exploited innocents for his products. He's even referred to as "Wonka Rick" by the fanbase. Faux Affably Evil: He's more polite than the average Rick and can appeal to Rick J-22's humanity to calm him down; he's also willing to lock up fellow Ricks in aLotus-Eater Machineforprofit.

characters.name: RickJ19ζ7/ Doofus Rick
characters.description: A Rick whom the other Ricks pick on for being unlike the other Ricks: He's a kindhearted bonehead who strikes up a friendship with Jerry. Then again the guy knows a formula that makes edible brownies from non-edible chemicals without the use of an oven. He also eats his own crap. Allegedly. All of the Other Reindeer: He gets picked on by the other Ricks for being the onlyNice Guyof the bunch. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: In the comics, it's revealed that he invented theCure for Cancerin his universe. Ambiguous Situation: Despite Doofus Rick stating that he never married and has kids, andThe Revealthat all versions of Diane have beenRet-Gonedue to Rick Prime's Omega Device, it's not unknown if Dimension J19ζ7 has a native Diane (who was then wiped from existence) or not. The Anti-Nihilist: Like other Ricks, he believes that life is "dangerous and complex and unyielding," but while other Ricks choose to use this as an excuse to inflict cruelty on whoever they need to for the brief aggrandizement of themselves, Doofus Rick does the opposite, reasoning that even just trying to get by is winning in and of itself.

characters.name: Hammerhead Morty
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Object: He has a hammer for a head. The Bus Came Back: He first shows up as one of the many captured Morties in the Season 1 finale. He later returns in Season 3 "Rickshank Redemption" where he gets used by a Rick in the Citadel's battle against the Galactic Federation. Human Shield: He is used by one Rick as a shield against a Galactic Federation guard's gunfire. Living Weapon: During the battle between the Citadel and the Galactic Federation, one Rick uses him to smash several Galactic Federation prisoners along with being aHuman Shieldbefore said Rick gets killed. Metal Muncher: According to theOfficial Character Guide, after his death a Galactic Federation autopsy found nails among his stomach contents. TheGuidethen proceeds to immediatelylampshadethe absoluteboatloadofinvokedFridge Logicthis raises.

characters.name: Commander Rick
characters.description: Grand Theft Me: He has his body stolen by Rick C-137 to infiltrate the Citadel. Uncertain Doom: Our RickBody Surfsinto this Rick and then using Commander Rick's body orders his old one to be killed claiming him to be a spy. It's uncertain if this was carried out or not. We Hardly Knew Ye: Hemay or may not have diedin his first scene.

characters.name: Rick J- 22 / "Factory Rick"
characters.description: A Rick who — despite apparently having the same IQ as the other Ricks — has been reduced to the role of a menial worker at a confection factory. He eventually snaps, killing his boss and holding Simple Rick hostage in exchange for a portal gun — hoping to escape the Citadel once and for all. Almighty Janitor: Intelligent enough to improvise a weapon out of broken factory equipment and devious enough to recognize the "blender dimension" trap on sight, J-22 is clearly just as brilliant as the main Rick... and yet he's trapped in a boring job that could probably be performed by a monkey. And the same goes for just about all the other Ricks doing menial work for the Citadel. Ambiguous Situation: He pushes Simple Rick through the portal from the portal gun he was given, only for it to kill him via blender dimension trap. J-22's words afterwords could mean either he suspected this outcome or is simply mad that they tried to do that to a fellow Rick, so it's hard to say if he wanted to save Simple Rick or was simply using him to test the portal. Going Postal: The action in J-22's plot begins when he finally snaps after years of demeaning work with no opportunities for promotion, tearing a piece of machinery off the assembly line and using it to murder his boss. Hope Spot: After almost being arrested/killed by Rick policemen in a standoff, Rick D. Sanchez III, the factory's owner, escorts him out safely with the other citizens cheering him on. Outside, he is offered a car with the keys, and as he walks towards it while smiling,Rick D. Sanchez III shoots him in the back of the head with a stun gun.

characters.name: Rick C-60/Simple Rick
characters.description: A Rick with a notable absence of lofty ambitions in science and a great love for his family. His endorphins also happen to be the main ingredient in a popular candy franchise named after him. A version of him first appeared in the false memory of C-137 during his interrogation by the Galactic Federation. Cruel Twist Ending: To his personal story at least. His dedication to his family leads to him getting abducted by Wonka Rick and placed in aLotus-Eater Machine, to have his brain fluids, which were perfect for use as an ingredient in his candy, drained. And then...he ultimately faces a really messy death, being killed by a trap meant for another Rick. Family Versus Career: He chose family over science. Unfortunately, it ended up dooming him through no fault of his own. Foreshadowing:His origin is stated to be off the Central Finite Curve alludes to what it actually is, a few seasons before it becomes relevant.It's a collection of universes in which Rick is the smartest man in the universe, hence Ricks like Simple Rick only exist outside of it.Also, the fact that he's aGood Counterpartwhose life is ruined by his malicious and amoral multiverse counterparts sets up the eventual reveal ofRick C-137's true origins. His origin is stated to be off the Central Finite Curve alludes to what it actually is, a few seasons before it becomes relevant.It's a collection of universes in which Rick is the smartest man in the universe, hence Ricks like Simple Rick only exist outside of it.

characters.name: Rookie Rick and Officer Morty
characters.description: A Rick and Morty part of the Citadel's police force. Boomerang Bigot: Officer Morty thinks very low of Rickless Mortys, even though he's Rickless himself, and goes ballistic when someone claims he's a sidekick to his partner Rick. Brutal Honesty: Officer Morty doesn't really bother with metaphors.Officer Morty:This is Big Morty, he helps us keep the peace in Mortytown. Think of him as "a drug lord" and us as "cops on his payroll." By-the-Book Cop: It's pretty clear that Police Rick is fresh out of police training and thus often tries to stick to what he learned during that time. Dirty Cop: Officer Morty treats his fellow Mortys like animals and takes bribes from Big Morty, a gang leader.

characters.name: Rick D716, D716-B, and D716-C/Reporter Rick
characters.description: A group of Ricks who report the news for the Citadel. Clone Degeneration: A dimensional variant. Rick D716 looks normal, but D716-B has a disfigured scar down his right eye. He quips that it "must be nice" when the original introduces himself as just plain Rick D716.Both of themlook down on Rick D716-C, whose entire right half of his face is horribly disfigured and whose right eye is lower than the left.D716-B:That fucking guy...D716:Tell me about it. Deadpan Snarker: Rick is still Rick, so even when reporting the news, they'll throw in their disdain for the topic. Kent Brockman News: Like many Ricks, these Ricks are clearly biased against Morty, as they openly make fun of the Morty running for President. While showing footage of his campaign, they mock him by thinking his speech was about how he was clearly going to lose. Screw This, I'm Out of Here!: Rick D716 goes on air during an emergency just to mock his viewers, admits he was paid millions by the drug companies to say every word, and flat-out states he doesn't care whether his viewers live or die before bailing.Given that the emergency is Evil Morty hacking the Citadel's portal supply so it leads to places that instantly kill anyone trying to escape, Rick D716 is immediately murdered by a monster that emerges from his portal.Rick D716-B then nonchalantly takes his place and encourages viewers to buy prescription drugs.

characters.name: Slick Morty, Reptile Morty, Glasses Morty, and Fat Morty
characters.description: Four Mortys who journeyed into the outskirts of the newly-constructed Citadel to search for the fabled Wishing Portal. Be Careful What You Wish For: Slick Morty's wish in the Wishing Portal is for things to change in the Citadel. ThenEvil Morty becomes President and takes over the Shadow Council of Ricks, which is probably goingFrom Bad to Worse. Bus Crash:Fat Morty is among the many dead Ricks and Mortys floating around in space after the Citadel's destruction, as shown in the opening of "Solaricks". Covert Pervert: Glasses Morty, whose wish is that incest porn had more mainstream appeal.For a friend. Drama Queen: Slick Morty, which is justified since he's part of an experimental line of Mortys with a "drama implant".Slick:How do you think it feels, Fat Morty? To know that no matter where I go, I'll always be the one that makes everyone sad... and a little bored.

characters.name: Campaign Manager Morty
characters.description: A Morty in charge of helping his presidential candidate Morty get elected. Conspicuously Public Assassination:He tries to kill Candidate Morty in public, but he fails. The Eeyore: He kept telling Candidate Morty to throw in the towel and quit since he didn't believe that he had a chance. Candidate Morty eventually fired him after he exceeded everyone's expectations and succeeded by going against his advice. His Name Is...: After getting fired by his candidate, he learns that the Morty he was trying to get elected was actuallyEvil Morty and tries to assassinate him, but fails and gets jettisoned into space before he can spill the beans. Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!: After receiving intelligence that Candidate Mortyis actually Evil Morty, he decides to try and assassinate him in public. Not only does he fail to kill Evil Morty, but in doing so possibly got him elected out of sympathy for the botched assassination. He's then spaced before he can reveal the secret to anyone else.

characters.name: Trenchcoat Rick
characters.description: A mysterious Rick who provides Campaign Manager Morty with shocking information about Candidate Morty. He Knows Too Much:Most likely why Evil Morty killed him. Killed Offscreen:Sometime after providing Campaign Manager Morty with the information about Candidate Morty's identity, Trenchcoat Rick isThrown Out the Airlock(presumably becauseHe Knows Too Much), as his already-dead body is seen floating in space around the Citadel along with all the other Rick and Morty corpses. Mysterious Informant: He's the one who provides Campaign Manager Morty with evidence thatCandidate Morty is Evil Morty. How and where he himself got it is never revealed. Unwitting Instigator of Doom: Him giving Campaign Manager Morty the information aboutCandidate Morty's true identityinadvertently sets off a chain of events that would result inCandidate Morty winning the election, Campaign Manager Morty getting killed trying to warn the rest of the Citadel, and the events of the Season 5 finale.

characters.name: Big Morty
characters.description: A druglord Morty who runs a strip club known as The Creepy Morty. Boom, Headshot!: How Officer Morty kills him. If You're So Evil, Eat This Kitten!: He threatens to kill Rookie Rick unless he takes the offered bribe money. Mister Big: He's called Big Morty despite being as short as most Mortys.Lampshadedin an exchange with Officer Morty.Officer Morty:Not so big now, are you?Big Morty:I never was! It was figurative! Porn Stache: He has a wispy mustache that's only half grown in. It helps emphasize both his sliminess and the sliminess of the business he runs.

characters.name: Slow Rick/Tall Morty
characters.description: A dimwitted Rick who is convinced he's a Morty. Book Dumb: Can't even pronounce "graduate" correctly. Held Back in School: He's never picked as a Morty. The implication from the teacher's slip in calling him "Slow Rick" is that the other Ricks dumped him there for safekeeping and don't plan to ever let him out.

characters.name: Big Rick
characters.description: Big Bad Wannabe: He's the top dog of an empire that's already been toppled and whose resources are scant, but is otherwise content to just boss around his fellow Ricks and Mortys. Catchphrase: Big Rick's "Get yo' mouth round it!" Since he was cloned to be the mascot of a gumbo restaurant chain, this phrase is presumably the restaurant's slogan. Homesteader Rickrepeats itback at himat the end before destroying the proto-Citadel. Chair Reveal: Big Rick gets introduced being turned around in his chair by a Morty-powered crank. Concealing Canvas: Big Rick hides his emergency portal fluid in a safe behind a gallery piece in his office. Crazy-Prepared: Big Rick has a gun built into his desk in case any backstabbers try to steal his back-up portal fluid, as the lead Trafficker Rick finds out the hard way.

characters.name: Oddjob Rick
characters.description: The Dragon: The most distinct Rick minion working for Big Rick. Expy: To Oddjob fromGoldfinger. Non-Standard Character Design: He's got a wider, more muscular frame than the other Ricks due to being a bodyguard instead of a scientist. Tear Off Your Face: Oddjob Rick dies from one of Homesteader Rick's drones tearing off his face. Uncomfortable Elevator Moment: Oddjob Rick tries to make small talk with the lead Trafficker Rick to bridge the long, awkward silence of their elevator ride up to Big Rick's office, asking if he likes football. Trafficker Rickisn't interested in chatting.

characters.name: Trafficker Ricks
characters.description: Establishing Character Moment: The lead Trafficker Rick's first scene on his own has him meet with Big Rick and act thoroughly indifferent and unenthused towards the latter's plans for the new Citadel, setting him up to eventually try to betray Big Rick later because he doesn't actually feel any loyalty toward his "boss" or what he's working towards. Trafficker Rick also, on his way out of the penthouse, knocks a tray out of one of the servant Mortys' handsjust because he can, making it clear that he may not be loyal to Big Rick, but he's definitely still a bad guy. Failed a Spot Check: The trafficker Rick clones who raid Mortytown near the beginning presumably intend to capture every Morty clone there, and we even see them breaking into the other buildings in the town and taking the Mortys who live there. But after Homesteader Rick exits the arcade (the biggest building on the street) and they riddle him with bullets, the Trafficker Ricks don't even bother to check if there are any more Mortys hiding in there before torching the place. As it turns out, thereweretwo of them, Arcade Morty and Doc, who ultimately escape the flames and end up joining Homesteader Rick's attack on the Citadel so they can save their friends. Karmic Death: They mocked Homesteader Rick for enjoingTori Amos. In the climax of the episode, Homesteader Rick wipes them all out while "Little Earthqukes" plays overhead. Kick the Dog: Not only do the Citadel Ricks casually gun down Homesteader Rick in the street for a laugh, they make sure to backtrack to the farm he built justto burn it to the ground,brutally kill his beloved petandmake fun of his Tori Amos collection. Pistol-Whipping: The lead Trafficker Rick hits Arcade Morty in the head with his pistol and tells him to shut up after the latter shouts for Homesteader Rick not to go through with Big Rick's request to make more clones. And a moment before that, Big Rick clubs Homesteader Rick in the back of the head with his cane for no real reaso

characters.name: Homesteader Rick
characters.description: Animal Lover: While not especially hospitable around people, he at least seems to take care of his farm animals well, even giving one of his sick animals space to avoid infecting the others while eating in peace. He gets royally pissed off when the Citadel Ricks decide to murder them all just for kicks, and goes on aRoaring Rampage of Revengein response. An Arm and a Leg: Oddjob Rick slices off Homesteader Rick's arm with his bladed hat. At Least I Admit It: Homesteader Rick, who was originally the Citadel's lead Morty-cloning scientist, is well aware that he's not a good person and is fairly blunt about it. Once Arcade Morty finds out about his past and begins angrily yelling at him, Rick just responds that he never said he was a good guy. And right before he creates the giant Morty clone to attack the clone Ricks (whom he also contributed to creating), he fully acknowledges that he's just as bad of a person as them, but at leasthehas the self-awareness to be ashamed of how terrible they all are:Homesteader Rick: Kid's right. I'm no better than any of you. I'm just self-loathing about it. The Atoner: Downplayed.
