He's revealed to have been the original Citadel's former head scientist in charge of Morty cloning, making him one of the biggest perpetuators of the Citadel's horrifying system of mass-producing Mortys asExpendable Clones. Arcade Morty is understandably disgusted to learn this. By the present, Homesteader Rick isn't actively trying to help or make things better for the clones he created, just wants to live a life of solitude in peace, and him attacking the Rick clones' new Citadel has nothing to do with saving the Morty clones they kidnapped and is entirely motivated byRevenge. Still, it's obvious that Rick feels a lot of shame and self-loathing about the role he played, and unlike the clone Ricks, he doesn't see the Morty clones as subhuman. Ultimately, he does end up helping Arcade Morty rescue them, and pulls aRedemption Equals DeathLast Stand so they c

characters.name: Arcade Morty
characters.description: Borrowed Biometric Bypass: Arcade Morty uses a dead Rick's hand on a biometric scanner to unlock the prison cell the Mortys are kept in. Due to the Dead: Once he moves into the now-deceased Homesteader Rick's old farm, Arcade Morty puts up headstones for both Rick and Doc, a Morty clone who also died in the proto-Citadel attack. He doesn't actually have either of their bodies to bury there, both of which were destroyed in the Citadel's collapse, so it's purely symbolic. Fake Memories: Like all Morty clones. He has the same memory as Doc of his "former Rick" going to the park with him, though he at least knows it's fake. At the end, on Homesteader Rick's advice, he helps the other clones find their place so they can make their own memories. Mirror Character: Like many other variants, he's one to Morty Prime (the series' main Morty):When surrounded by large groups of other Mortys, both of them are easily the most active, assertive, and competent Mortys in the room and show some exasperation towards their variants' meekness and incompetence. Nevertheless, they truly don't want to see harm come to other versions of themselves and do their best to save them, as seen with Morty Prime in "Close Rick-Counters" and in this episode with Arcade Morty being determined to save his Mortytown friends.Both of them see an alternate version of themselves (an artificially-created one, at that) get fatally shot in front of them, and hold and attempt to comfort them as they die. (For Morty Prime, it was his aged-up self in "Rickmurai Jack", and here, it's Arcade Morty's friend Doc.)Both Mortys are also far more world-weary and much more assertive towards their Rick companions than most other Mortys are, not willing to take nearly as much crap from them. They each discover the dark roles that their respective Ricks played in the Citadel's broken system, and are horrified, angry, and disgusted at first, but are soon able to forgive them. Main Morty forgave his Rick after learning the rest

characters.name: "Doc"
characters.description: Chekhov's Gunman: A minor example. When Homesteader Rick comes into the Mortytown arcade, Arcade Morty speaks to another Morty called "Doc", whom we don't actually see and just hear his voice offscreen. Doc ends up being the only other Morty besides Arcade Morty who doesn't get kidnapped by the trafficker Ricks, and hitches a ride along with him on Homesteader Rick's truck to save their friends. However, Doc does end up getting fatally shot fairly early on in the rescue mission and doesn't get to accomplish much before he dies. Died in Your Arms Tonight: Dies in Arcade Morty's arms after being shot in the chest by one of the clone Ricks. Fake Memories: Like most if not all Morty clones, Doc has these, which cause him to remember his "previous" Rick (who never even existed) as someone who was fairly nice and regularly took him and Summer to the park. Heroic Sacrifice: During the Citadel shooutout, he mostly hangs back nervously while Homesteader Rick and Arcade Morty do the shooting, but when the latter is grabbed and choked by a muscular Rick clone, Doc gathers his courage and jumps on the clone's back to save his friend. He succeeds, but it does get him quickly shot through the chest for his effort, andhe dies in Arcade Morty's arms. Irony: This Morty is meant to be aMarty McFlyexpy, yet he is named "Doc".

characters.name: The Space Cruiser
characters.description: Rick's home-built space ship he made out of car parts, and the associated A.I. that controls it and acts as its security system. It is completely obedient to Rick and as well as anyone Rick tells it to protect. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Averted. While most people would consider a security system that immediately kills anything it considers a threat to be deemed a mistake of bad programming, considering thatRickcreated it, her homicidal programming is most likely intentional. Ax-Crazy: As if not evident enough in her first major appearance, her second one has her killing aPlanet Eaterfor sport, killing a bunch of Changeformers for mocking her for being just a ship, killing a human and using her body as a meat puppet, blowing up an interstellar police station, and taking pride in being an all powerful war machine. Badass Boast: After releasing a decaying clone of a SWAT officer's deceased child:"All of you have loved ones. All of them can be returned. All can be taken away." Batman Gambit: In "Amortycan Grickfitti" she goes offline after Morty and Summer trick her with aLogic Bomb. After the two have used her to cause enough trouble, the AI reveals she was faking the entire time and gathered enough evidence of their exploits that now she can do everything she wants to do then blame the entire thing on Morty and Summer.

characters.name: Garage
characters.description: Rick's garage serves as the primary workshop. It has an AI, similar to the Space Cruiser. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Averted. Able to revive Jerry and Rick albeit with some difficulty. Ambiguously Related: Their similar behaviors and same voice actress imply a relation to the AI in Rick's Space Cruiser, but it isn't entirely clear if it's a similar, but separate AI from the one in the Space Cruiser, or is the same AI able to transfer between the two "bodies." Deadpan Snarker: Audibly sighs when seeing Jerry and Rick's mind and brains scrambled.Garage AI:There goes my Thursday. Dirty Coward: Tries to get Neighbor Glen to provide energy storage devices when Rick is unconscious in Birdperson's mind.

characters.name: Gearhead
characters.description: A somewhat shady and cowardly acquaintance of Rick from a civilization of mechanical beings. He doesn't like to be called "Gearhead". Ambiguously Bi: Gearhead was heavily implied to be gay through his effeminate voice and gestures, and the fact that he apparently owns a gay magazine that could be seen in his workshop. However, he was seen flirting with a couple of college-aged gear girls in the post-credits scene of "Vindicators 3" Back for the Dead: He returns in "Vindicators 3: The Return of Worldender" only totrip while retreating from his lie of being a Vindicator, falling apart in the process. The Bore: In his initial appearance he'd bore anyone who would listen to him about the Gear Wars no matter how little they cared. The Bus Came Back: He reappears at the end andcredits sceneof "Vindicators 3: The Return of Worldender", twelve episodes since his previous appearance in "Mortynight Run".

characters.name: Birdperson/Phoenixperson
characters.description: Rick's best friend who is introduced attending Rick's house party looking for a new mate after breaking up with his previous soul-partner spirit-bond. And he's a superhero of some sort being called to said party via a beacon. Aliens Steal Cable: Rick mentioned once that Birdperson annually holds viewing parties for the Oscars, but...Rick:By the way, our TV signals take light years to reach his planet. Nobody tell him that Braveheart wins! Atrocious Alias: Tammy isn't exactly jazzed about his new moniker of Phoenixperson.Rick, Beth and her clone share the same sentiment. Back from the Dead:He is truly resurrected in "Rickternal Friendshine of the Rickless Mort", after Rick reconstitutes his original body and helps a memory of Birdperson become a sentient being. Bash Brothers: He and Rick served were this in the past when they waged war against the Galactic Federation. The apex of this is their fight against the Gromflomites at Blood Ridge.

characters.name: Squanchy
characters.description: One of Rick's closest friends, Squanchy is a cat-like alien from the planet Squanch. Caught with Your Pants Down: Morty and Jessica catch himsquanchingin a closet during "Ricksy Business". Crouching Moron, Hidden Badass: He may look like a silly cartoon character with a high-pitched voice and a goofy speech pattern, but if the situation gets grim, he's perfectly able toturn into a 15 feet tall hulking beastwhile retaining his awareness and tear through mooks while shrugging off lasers. A Friend in Need: Distracts the Federation Forces so that Rick and his family can escape a shootout.Squanchy: There's no time to squanch, get your family out of here! I got this! Hulking Out: He has some kind of liquid in one of his teeth that turns him into a huge beast.

characters.name: Slow Mobius
characters.description: An alien with the power to manipulate time. Back for the Dead: Slow Mobius was completely absent between Season 1 and Season 7, only reappearing so that Rick Prime could demonstrate how cruel he was by killing someone all Ricks cared about (including Rick Prime himself). C-List Fodder: Even calling him "c-list" is a stretch - he appeared once in Season 1 as a simple gag character, with no indication that he was particularly close to Rick. When Rick Prime decides to erase Rick's family one by one in "Mortricken", it turns out that he considered Slow Mobius his belovedHonorary Uncleand starts with him, leaving Rick horrified and distraught. Deader than Dead: Rick Prime executes Slow Mobius using a device that would simultaneously kill all of his multiversal variants. Honorary Uncle: Rick affectionately refers to him as "Uncle Slow".

characters.name: Mr. Poopybutthole
characters.description: One of the many new characters that show up after the parasites get into the house. He is a diminutive yellow rod-shaped being dressed in a light blue shirt, knee-high blue pants, brown shoes and a blue-rimmed top-hat. Alien Blood: Subverted. The fact that he has red blood when shot by Beth is aWham Shotshowing that he is not one of the malevolent parasites. All There in the Manual: The showrunners, when pressed, did eventually give him an origin story in an interview that crosses intoDon't Explain the Joketerritory:he's a more benign and advancedEnergy Beingform of the brain parasites that feeds by forming real friendships with lower lifeforms. The easiest way for him to do so is to insert himself into the lives of lifeforms that have experienced memory loss or alteration.This appears to have been overcome by later events as the character took on a larger role in the show and had his backstory developed. Babies Ever After:The Stingerfor the season 3 finale reveals he got himself cleaned up and has a wife and kid. Breakout Character: Similar to Mr. Meeseeks, he was a memorably zany character that got a positive reception and even reappeared inThe Stingersfor the finales of seasons 2 and 3, has made numerous cameo appearances, and returns for a substantial role in a season four episode.

characters.name: Two Crows
characters.description: Two crows randomly picked by Rick to be his new sidekicks to punish Morty for screwing up. Morality Chain: Surprisingly they end up being this for Rick. During an adventure where Rick tries to get an alien treasure from a temple and ignores a bunch of ridiculously cute aliens being murdered by a temple trap, the crows stop Rick from getting the idol because "empathy is the real treasure." Rick first tries to fire them only for alien crows to teach him empathy and eventually decides to see what more they can teach him. Rebound Best Friend: Rick makes them his new sidekicks after Morty makes one mistake too many. At first it's just a bit, but after learning how empathetic they are, he actually becomes super obsessed with crows and decides to make the change permanent. He even tries to start a new franchise: Rick and Two Crows, where theyWalk the Earthfacing down the forces of their nemesis, Crow Scare. Except then it turns out the crows are using Rick as a rebound for Crow Scare, who turns out to be their old adventuring partner and they end up dumping Rick to get back together with their ex. Uplifted Animal: An artifact owned by the crow aliens briefly allows them to transform into similar aliens, only for the two crows to go back to normal after helping Rick destroy it. The only thing they ask for in return is bird quaaludes. We Can Rule Together: The two crows are given this offer by the alien crows, who turn on Rick once they find out he thought crows were stupid. The crows play along long enough to become like the alien crows, then use their skills to save Rick's life instead.

characters.name: Reuben
characters.description: A homeless man whose internal organs were used by Rick to create a miniature theme park. Disposable Vagrant: The microscopic theme park built inside him is just the beginning. Monstrous Germs: The various diseases that live in Reuben's body are hideous monsters that look nothing like real germs. Some at least show a resemblance to actual bacteria or viruses, but usually the wrong type (Tuberculosis is portrayed as orb-shaped when it should be rod-shaped, and E. coli, a bacterium, looks like abacteriophage virus), and then there are the Hepatitis viruses that seem to be designed after theRancoror theCloverfieldmonster. No Dead Body Poops: Averted; Dr. Bloom notes that the sphincter dam, constructed when Reuben became incontinent, was not designed to hold back a corpse-load. The dam eventually bursts and floods the area with excrement, killing Roger. Ominous Floating Spaceship: Reuben's giant corpse casts a menacing shadow all over the whole continental US.

characters.name: Dr. Xenon Bloom
characters.description: An amoeba-like creature who co-founded Anatomy Park. He ends up getting killed by a swarm of E. coli while operating a train to save Morty and Annie. Bad Boss: Apart from holding an amusement park with potentially life-threatening risks, but according to Poncho, Bloom gives out iTunes gift cards as aHoliday bonus. Expy: OfJohn Hammond. He even has a near-identical walking stick. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He comes off as an unsettling fellow, especially given hissurroundingsandexpertise, but still at least tries to be friendly and cheerful. Punny Name: His name is one onJeff Goldblum, since xenon and gold are both chemical elements.

characters.name: Krombopulos Michael
characters.description: A trigger-happy yetextremely personableassassin that Rick sells guns to. Aerith and Bob: A rare example of this trope applying to one character. "Michael" is a decidedly normal last name for an alien namedKrombopulos. This seems to apply to their entire species, given in the next season we have Cornvelious Daniel. Affably Evil: It is really hard to hate an assassin who absolutely loves his job, is the friendliest guy you'll ever meet when he's off the clock, and hands out his business card while wishing you a good day.Krombopulos:Oh boy, here I go killing again! An Alien Named "Bob": Played with. His first name is Krombopulos, but his last name is the mundane human first name "Michael". Ax-Crazy: The Vindicators comic series shows that not only does he openly murder practically everyone he meets, not killing for extended amounts of time will throw him into severe fits of depression.

characters.name: Jaguar
characters.description: An assassin sent out by the agency he was held captive in to kill Pickle Rick. Androcles' Lion: Saves Rick and Morty in the Stinger after the former helped him take down the Agency Director. Big Damn Heroes: Appears inThe Stingerof "Pickle Rick" to save Rick and Morty from Concerto. Boxed Crook: The Agency Director offers Jaguar and his daughter, Caterina, their freedom, if Jaguar can kill Pickle Rick. Dark Is Not Evil: Jaguar wears a black bodysuit and has a horrifying appearance, but he is fighting against corrupt government officials and even saves Rick and Morty from Concerto.

characters.name: Balthromaw
characters.description: A dragon that was enslaved by a Wizard and sold to Morty, but ends up bonding with Rick. Actor Allusion: The incident with Rick mentioned below is a clear reference toGame of Throneswhere Quentyn Martell attempts to tame Rheagar the dragon and gets burned alive for his trouble. Liam Cunningham plays The Onion Knight, Ser Davos Seaworth, in the series. Breath Weapon: Naturally, he can breathe fire. Rick even points this out when heNo Sellshis flames.Rick:If only I had prepared better for this encounter by remembering the only thing dragons are known for! Does This Remind You of Anything?: Subverted. After using it as a metaphor for sex the entire episode,Synchronizationwith multiple people/dragons at once is explicitly labelled an orgy. Flight: The other thing dragons are known for. Notably the ability to ride him is why Morty wants a dragon in the first place, but Balthromaw finds flying as tedious as a human might find walking a marathon.

characters.name: Bigfoot
characters.description: TheBigfoot, who is revealed to be continuously antagonized by Rick. Bigfoot, Sasquatch, and Yeti: He's Bigfoot. Body Backup Drive: When Bigfoot joins the resurrection cycle after being killed by the Pope, he's initially dropped into a copy of Summer before Rick engineers him a unique human body. Foreshadowing: He's forshadowed via a picture drawn by a supposed psychic hired by the President in "Air Force Wong", showing Rick being attacked by Bigfoot. Grievous Harm with a Body: Bigfoot tries and fails numerous methods to breach the Project Phoenix pod before finally whaling on it with Rick's corpse in frustration. Unfortunately, whatever Rick's cybernetic implants are made of is tough enough to damage the reinforced glass.

characters.name: Salvatron
characters.description: Robot drones tasked with sorting through Rick's garbage. Distracted by the Sexy: They get distracted by the remains of Morty's sex-bot Gwendolyn. Failed a Spot Check: Salvatron's scanning tech is limited towards spotting movement, rather than detecting body heat or pulses. This allows morty and Morty Jr. to evade them twice. Punch-Clock Villain: Salvatron only tries to kill Morty, Morty Jr., and the trash robots because if Rick knew that anything valuable in his garbage had been allowed to fester long enough to form a civilization, he'd punish Salvatron for letting things get that far.

characters.name: Unity
characters.description: A hive-minded, intangible being and an old fling of Rick's. Affably Evil: Plans to take over the Universe and eliminate free will. It is also really, really nice to both Rick and his grandchildren, and at least one planet has been significantly improved by it taking over. All Girls Want Bad Boys:Deconstructed. Unity is attracted toRick, but his influence on it causes it to lose control over the species it's taken control over. Unity ultimately decides that they can't be together because, unlike it, Rickcan'tchange. Ambiguous Gender: Unity is a genderless entity that is capable of possessing male and female bodies alike. However, during its screentime in "Auto Erotic Assimilation", while it uses and speaks through many bodies of both genders, we see it speaking through female bodies more, and the "primary" body that it uses as the "leader" of the world it's assimilated is also female. It had a relationship with Rick, but since he's pansexual, it doesn't matter to him what gender Unity is; however, when he's having sex with many different redheaded bodies it's possessing, we see more female redheads than males. Amicable Exes: When they return in "Air Force Wong", Unity tries to be this with Rick, saying they only invaded Virginia because they were worried about him after hearing thathe's going after Rick Prime, since he was nearly killed the last time he tried. Though they want to remain friends, Rick doesn't, and his actions end with Unity being unable to trust him by the end of the episode.

characters.name: BugAnne
characters.description: A member of Space Beth's resistance who engages in a sexual relationship with Rick. Ascended Extra:BugAnnestarts out as aLiving Propin Space Beth's sidestories. Once she takes notice of Rick's devotion to his daughter, she develops an attraction to him and she's next seen sleeping with him. Friend with Benefits: She has this sort of relationship with Rick, enjoying their nights in the bedroom while having some history together as fellow rebels. She understands Rick's fear of commitment due to still not being over his dead wife Diane so she is fine keeping it casual between them. Green-Skinned Space Babe: She looks like an attractive human lady with insectoid features, no surprise when Rick falls for her. Any dragon who is caught being with another person is deemed a "slut", as far as the wizard is concerned, especially if soul-bounding is involved.

characters.name: Talking Cat
characters.description: A mysterious talking cat that Jerry meets in his room out of nowhere and who refuses to give explanations. Cats Are Mean: Somewhatdownplayedinitially; At worst, he's merely a socially-ineptJerkasswho comes off as more creepy and insufferable than outright malicious or mean-spirited. But apparently whatever gave him the ability to speak is so monstrously, incomprehensibly evil that even Rick is almost driven to suicide by it. Diabolus ex Nihilo: He just shows up offscreen in Jerry's room. Rick even says him showing up is completely unrelated to his adventures with Morty. Flat Character: Intentionally so. He is inexplicably obsessed with maintaining only two random character traits; avoiding questions about why he can talk and partying in Florida. Even when no one cares about why he can speak and he's kicked out of Florida, he still dedicates himself to these obsessions. Hypocrite: He tells Jerry that he shouldn't ask questions and he should just focus on having fun. But on the Florida party cruise, he repeatedly asks questions of the other guests, bringing down the entire party to the point where the partygoers kick him off the cruise.

characters.name: Alien Snakes
characters.description: A society from a planet of snakes in the brink of a world war. Enemy Mine: Discovering that there are other forms of life in the universe is enough for them to (for the most part) put their differences aside and band together to attack Earth. Fantastic Racism: Apparently their entire planet is in one big snake race war, although from what we are shown of their society, different species of snake get along just fine. High Collar of Doom: The President of the country that sent their first astronaut to space has the collar of his suit turned up and extending past his head, resembling a cobra's hood. Kill All Humans: After Morty sends a snake from a pet store to their planet as aReplacement Goldfishfor their astronaut snake, they find out about the dangers humans pose to their kind and decide to wage war.

characters.name: Hoovans
characters.description: A Race of Cow-Like creatures that live in a dimension that has an accelerated time compared to ours. All for Nothing: What their main goal ultimately boils down to. Morty legitimately never meant the Hoovans any harm, and the entire vendetta against him was based off of a simple misunderstanding. And despite the Hoovans spending literal millennia training every generation to fight back against the “Dark Child”, they are ultimately defeated the moment Rick and Mr. Nimbus get involved, meaning they’ve waged a millennia-long, one-sided war for nothing. Anti-Villain: The Hoovans that are given focus are presented as cruel and conniving, but they have been indoctrinated from birth into a culture of revenge with their only purpose in life being to wait for Morty's return even when his visits are spaced several lifetimes apart for them. Arch-Enemy: Their entire society has been dedicated to destroying Morty in retaliation for his many unintentional crimes. Cassandra Truth: Because the gaps between Morty's appearances are so long from their perspective, many of the Hoovans believe that the "Dark Child" is nothing but a myth. Only after Morty leaves behind one of Rick's weapons (allowing them to advance their society considerably) is his existence universally accepted.

characters.name: Arabic Man
characters.description: A wealthy Arabic man who tried to purchase Planetina from the Tina-Teers. Arab Oil Sheikh: Lampshaded when he attacks Morty."I am an individual character, I represent no group!" Does This Remind You of Anything?: An evil Arabic man being killed bya group of seals. Exotic Entrée: He states his intention to eat infant seals to celebrate buying Planetina. Four Eyes, Zero Soul: He's bespeckled and a villain.

characters.name: Sperm Queen
characters.description: The leader of Morty's mutant sperm. Brick Joke: Her whole existence is meant to be payoff for a joke where the president and his cabinet act really sexist towards Summer, telling her they don't consider her useful unless they need a girl-on-girl fight. The Sperm Queen acknowledges that this would have been the most practical way to beat her. Oxymoronic Being: She's female, yet is a sperm, which are inherently male reproductive cells.

characters.name: Turkey President
characters.description: After the President transforms himself into a turkey as part of his ongoing feud with Rick, he ends up being switched with a random turkey that gets infused with his DNA and steals his identity. Armor-Piercing Question: After the Turkey President convinces Congress and his VP to let him remain President even after he's been exposed as a fake, the real President furiously asks them all if they think the imposter cares about America. The Turkey President, whose creation was the result of a petty feud between the real President and Rick, has a very effective response.POTUS: You can't be serious! You think he cares about America?!Turkey POTUS: Is that why this is happening to you? Because you cared about America? Creepy Monotone: Adding to his unnerving presence is his emotionless and stilted way of speaking. Presumably a side-effect of only recently learning how to speak like a human. Didn't Think This Through: He attempts to force aSadistic Choiceon the President. Either fight him, or allow the Turkey President's weapon on the Washington Monument to turn every turkey in America into super soldiers. The President points out the blindingly obvious solution is for him to kick the Turkey President's ass while Rick and Morty stop the weapon. Die Laughing: After being mortally wounded, he snaps his own wishbone and wishes to explode to take the President with him. His last moments are spent maniacally laughing before he blows up.

characters.name: Nick
characters.description: A man who got portal fluid splashed on his thigh that Morty finds himself connected to after getting some on his hand. After a falling out with Rick, Morty teams up with Nick to have new adventures as the "Portal Boys." Affably Evil: When Morty first meets him, Nick is very friendly, encouraging him to cut Rick out of his life because of how toxic their relationship is. He also discourages Morty from trying to bust him out of the mental institution he's locked in despite the horrifying abuse he suffers there. Once he gets his freedom back though, he quickly goes off the rails, murdering people who he thinks are crossing him and unarmed bystanders for fun. Even his friendliness to Morty ends after the latter abandons him. Ax-Crazy: It turns out there was a reason he was locked up in a mental institution. After Morty busts him out, it doesn't take long for Nick to start killing people at the drop of a hat. Bedlam House: The institution he's imprisoned in is this with guards who like to beat patients on Sundays. He says it's still better than Mondays when they tie them down and lick their faces.Plus it's meatloaf day. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He tells Morty he met Rick one night while drinking and then came home with him. He ended up messing with some stuff in the garage, got portal fluid splashed on him, then Rick literally fired him out of a catapult to Australia. The trauma ended up landing him in a mental institution. Later he reveals he was lying, Rick catapulted him because Nick tried to steal his portal gun, and given his killing spree later it's no mystery why he's locked up in an institution.

characters.name: Mr. Frundles
characters.description: A parasitic creature that Season 2 Jerry accidentally unleashes onto the world, forcing the Smith-Sanchez family to find a new dimension to live in. Adorable Abomination: Once the existential danger it presents becomes apparent it's undeniable that Mr. Frundles is an utterly adorable instance of the potential horrors in the wider universe. Apocalypse Wow: By the end of his screentime, Mr. Frundles has assimilated Earth itself, swallowing its oceans with its gigantic mouth and reducing it to a lifeless husk, thus being an example ofClass 6 of Apocalypse Wow. The Assimilator: Everything it bites acquires its face and the ability to bite other things to repeat the process. This can spread exponentially to quickly overtake a planet and everything on it. Clone by Conversion: Whatever it bites grows its face, verbally identifies as Mr. Frundles and bites other things to spread. Living things that already have a face will have them transformed into the same one it has.

characters.name: Jons
characters.description: The leader of a group of alien criminals who are staging aDie Hardheist on Blipz And Chitz, leaving it up to Summer to assume the role of JohnMcClaneand stop them. Contractual Genre Blindness: Since he's re-enactingDie Hard, his goons feel obligated to make the mistakes that they do in the films. Once he realizes that Summer Smith is "the ultimateMcClane" however, he immediately loses his cool and orders his terrorists to kill her no matter the cost.Jons:You don't have to not do things that were done inDie Hard. You can shoot the glass. Shoot the glass! Throw grenades! Do everything! Just kill her! Did Not Think This Through: Pulls aDie Hardagainst anintergalactic arcade, despite the fact that the entire place runs on tokens, and doesn't even have any money on-site. "Die Hard" on an X: Stages aDie Hardheist in a space arcade. Eaten Alive: Dies this way when one of his henchmen, Winslow, in a bizarreShout-Outto Officer Al Powell from the first movie, gets over his fear of eating people after having accidentally eaten a child some time before, and transforms into aOne-Winged Angelform and devours his boss.

characters.name: Jennith Padrow-Chunt
characters.description: The CEO of Fortune 500, a company that produces fortune cookies. Ambition Is Evil: She works every day towards fulfilling her cookie fortune of becoming the most successful businesswoman on earth, but she utilizes having that as an unfulfilled fortune to basically keep herself immortal and invulnerable. Bizarre Taste in Food: She is introduced in the introductory video for herself literally eating ramen noodles from a toilet, to illustrate what a loser she was prior to building her fortune cookie empire. Corrupt Corporate Executive: She the CEO of Fortune 500, and is willing to exploit the manipulation of fate for profit. Dropped a Bridge on Her: Her death by getting eaten by the Lockerean creature is rather unceremonious.

characters.name: Chuxley
characters.description: A crime boss whose goons unwittingly brought in Morty and was desperate to avoid facing the wrath of Rick Sanchez. Affably Evil: Despite being a crime boss, he is quite reasonable with his underlings and tries to avoid unnecessary conflict with Rick Sanchez. However, that does not mean he won't try to kill you and your family if you push him too far. Bullying the Dragon: At first, he tried his best to defy this when his goons brought in Morty for dealing crystals on their turf. He tries to assure Rick Sanchez that his grandson is perfectly fine and was even willing to throw in a bribe. However, seeing the confusing state Rick and Jerry were in made him think he could take them out which led to them mowing him and his gang down. He realizes this in the end, lamenting that he thought "I could kill God." Face Death with Dignity: He takes his death pretty well, all things considered, finding it an honor to die at the hands of Jerricky and accepting his last meal of a burger (pretty moldy) with grace. Genre Savvy: He is well aware that messing with Rick Sanchez is a death sentence. He berates his goons for bringing in Morty, the kid who hangs with Rick and tries his best to play nice with him. If it was Rick on any other day, it probably would just leave them alone.

characters.name: President of  41 Kepler B
characters.description: The President of a world where humanity produces spaghetti when they commit suicide. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She seems nice and kind, inviting Morty to her planet and offering for him to be a liaison between their worlds. However, she reveals herself to be a Cold, greedy capitalist willing to make thousands of her civilians kill themselves to satisfy the bottom line. Category Traitor: She sold out her own people as livestock. Further illustrating the point is that she's a woman of color. Even Evil Has Standards: Granted, it won’t stop her from profiting off of the suicide spaghetti trade, but even the President seems a littlegrossed outat the notion of eating her people’s intestines. Hate Sink: She's got absolutely no qualms about profiting off suicide or turning her entire planet into an industrial dystopia, caring only about the fiscal benefits.

characters.name: Kwyatt and Kenneth
characters.description: Leaders of an underground syndicate that traffics Kuatos. Big "NO!": Kenneth's Kuato (x several layers) when Rick uses his spider-like pod to force him to go into the ocean where he'll drown. Ear Ache: Morty bites Kenneth's ear off during their Kuato battle. Hunter of His Own Kind: The real mastermind behind the illegal Kuato trafficking is revealed to be Kenneth's Kuato...'s Kuato's Kuato. He openly admits to having sold out his own kind for money. Implausible Deniability: Kwyatt insists to Kenneth that he didn't betray him... though obviously he did lead Rick and Summer right to his lair.

characters.name: Oxygen-S/8/Infinity
characters.description: The mastermind behind the feud between the Alphabetrians and Numbericons. Conflict Killer: The destructive power Infinity has, along with killing his fellow Numbericons, convinced Sinistar-7 and the rest of the Numbericons to join forces with the Alphabetrians to stop him. Once Infinity is killed, the Alphabetrians and Numbericons broker a truce. Drunk with Power: Once 8 becomes Infinity, he begins killing everyone on Alphabetrium whether it's the Alphabetrians or the Numbericons. Evil Is Burning Hot: Upon ascending to Infinity, he changes from a reptilian cyborg to a fiery formation. The Mole: A Numbericon that altered his appearance so he could pass for an Alphabetrian.

characters.name: Lord Dreadnought
characters.description: The leader of the Numbericons. Big Bad Wannabe: He's killed immediately after his agent 8 ascends to Infinity. Expy: The cackling decimal point that hangs around him is reminiscent of Salacious Crumb, the alien monkey that Jabba the Hutt kept as a pet. His actual name, as revealed in the closed captioning, is indeed "Decimal Crumb". Punny Name: He is a sentient number 0, and his name is Lord Dreadnought. Shoulders of Doom: He wears an impressive set of pauldrons despite not having any arms.

characters.name: Easter Aliens aka Butt Guys
characters.description: A race of giants who wipe out civilizations by spreading concentrated pheromones that cause the population to breed themselves into ruin. Ancient Astronauts: Easter exists as part of a terraforming plot by aliens who the Easter Island heads are modeled after. Bizarre Alien Biology: Spoofed with the Easter Aliens having their butts on the front of their bodies and, to Rick's satisfied curiosity, their genitals on their backsides. They also appear to be made of some kind of jelly, as getting cut apart barely inconveniences them. Clipped-Wing Angel: The last surviving Easter Alien is subject to the were-bunny transformation, which already makes the subject superhumanly strong, and has nuclear-grade pheromonal abilities, but his transformation also makes him vulnerable to the fatal process of extracting the were-bunny essence. Expy: Of the Engineers from theAlienfilms. They're a race of pale, hairless humanoids who manufactured a virus that causesBody Horrorand is intended to weaponize sexual reproduction.

characters.name: James "Jimmy" Jamerson and Guffy Chachaco
characters.description: TwoHuman Aliensthat decide to rob their race while they're in cryo-sleep. Jimmy is the son of a wealthy family while Chachaco is the janitor. Cryonics Failure: Subverted when it's revealed Jimmy and Chachaco actually left stasis soon after the ship departed so they could rob the vault and shove monkeys in the pods to fake their deaths. Death by Materialism: The real Chachaco is ejected into space and dies because he prioritizes grabbing a valuable piece of hypercoal over securing himself to the ship's railing. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: Maybe not full "evil", but 11-year-old Jimmy’s definitely a greedy, selfishSpoiled Bratat best. However, hisIntergenerational Friendshipwith Guffy Chachaco does appear to be genuine despite the latter being part of the working class of their society, with Jimmy giving him a big hug after they hit the jackpot gambling and later letting out aBig "NO!"when Chachaco isThrown Out the Airlock. Chachaco in turn also cares about him. Last-Name Basis: Chachaco is almost never called by this first name, Guffy.

characters.name: The Trash of the Trash
characters.description: A robot formed from the discarded remains of Rick's various inventions that seeks to escape the garbage world. Big Bad Wannabe: It thought using Morty's DNA to get through security would be enough to escape. Turns out Rick anticipated at least two scenarios where that would seem suspicious, which immediately led to TOTT getting blasted by the Salvatron drones. Giant Scrap Robot: A hulking behemoth larger than any of the other trash bots that have been seen. Peripheral Heads: It has three heads, one of which is just a microwave. Politically Correct Villain: It expressed disgust with how Morty and Morty Jr. ranked their sexual conquests.

characters.name: Liu Sin
characters.description: A kung fu master that's a little too eager to deal out fatal retribution. Bad People Abuse Animals: Liu Sin likes using the Death Punch on everyone, including his master's cat Queef Richards. Can't Take Criticism: And you thoughtRickwas bad about this? Liu Sin will respond toanykind of pushback he gets, no matter how mild or minor, by using the Death Punch on the offender. Disproportionate Retribution: Liu Sin is a littletooeager to unleash the Death Punch on anyone who seemingly does anything as little as inconvenience him (such as just paying a little more for a TV-setup service)or even criticize him(as Morty finds out the hard way when he gets Death Punch'd). It turns out that he admits he can only connect through conflict (which seems to always end with him killing people). Easy Amnesia: Liu Sin hits Rick with an amnesia punch that causes him to forget who he is and which Beth is the clone (or rather, that he even knew which was which to begin with). Morty hits him with a "Ctrl+Z" punch to reset him.

characters.name: Pool Bot
characters.description: The Smiths' pool cleaner, which engages in an affair with Jerry. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: A simple software update turned this barely useful pool cleaner into a super-intelligent automaton capable of feeling jealousy and hatred. Almighty Janitor: The Pool Bot is not to be trifled with, as it's somehow incredibly capable enough to hack into the house's automated water faucets and even Rick's security system to trap Jerry and Keith inside while it fills the house with water to act like a slow but threatening shark. It Can Think: The pool bot is capable of having a romantic relationship with its (her?) human owner and has emoticons to react appropriately. This is a result of Jerry ignoring the warnings from theYouTubevideo and just installing the first firmware he finds. Yandere: The Pool Bot develops sentience and falls in love with Jerry. But when Jerry tries to break things off and hires Keith to clean the Pool instead, The Pool bot tries to murder Keith for supposedly getting in the way of it and Jerry's affair.

characters.name: Hog Resistance
characters.description: A resistance group that formed on a planet of pig people that Rick enslaved to supply him with alcohol. Anti-Villain: They wouldn't have provided any of the conflict in this episode if Rick didn't force their race to supply him with infinite booze. Brainwashed and Crazy:When the Hog Resistance calls Rick on the phone, he uses this to route the IT Cloud Entity there through the phone line to briefly possess the rebel leader's body instead. The newly commandeered hog then turns on his own resistance comrades,pipe in hand.The Resistance does this to Reese, who was originally programmed to only attack anything that threatens Rick, Morty, or the house, by rewiring him to become aKiller Robotwho's forced to try to kill the duo instead. When the Hog Resistance calls Rick on the phone, he uses this to route the IT Cloud Entity there through the phone line to briefly possess the rebel leader's body instead. The newly commandeered hog then turns on his own resistance comrades,pipe in hand. The Resistance does this to Reese, who was originally programmed to only attack anything that threatens Rick, Morty, or the house, by rewiring him to become aKiller Robotwho's forced to try to kill the duo instead.

characters.name: The Tree Warden
characters.description: A sentient tree that captures organisms and forces them to live through a constant cycle of birth, evolution and death. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: The sentient tree presents imprisonment in its ecosystem as a lesson in respect for the cycle of life. In reality, it's all a scam to trick them into fighting and killing each other so that the tree can feed on their dead bodies. Born-Again Immortality: The tree warden inflicts this on all its prisoners, keeping them all trapped in an endless cycle of death and rebirth, forcing them to reincarnate as amoebas every time they die and then having to evolve into other life forms from there. Greater-Scope Villain: It keeps people imprisoned in an endless cycle of death to feed itself. Although Rick ends up hated by most prisoners due to enslaving them all, they're willing to work with him because they hate the tree even more. Logical Weakness: For all that the tree stands above everyone else, it is still just as bound to the cycle of life as every single one of its prisoners. After Morty informs Rick of the true nature of it, he decides to gather every single prisoner into a closed cave to create an artificial biodome where they would live in through having Morty as a plant support their lifestyle. By the time the tree decides to check on what's happening, it's very weakened from the lack of nutrients.

characters.name: The Cat and Mouse Killer
characters.description: Asshole Victim: While it is brutal how the Police immediately opened fire on the Serial killer and blew him into mulch after he already surrendered, it was kind of deserved after all the countless people he murdered, which almost included Jerry. Ax-Crazy: As a Serial killer, he is basically this by default. He threatens to kill Jerry in disquieting ways once he found out he tricked him. Creepy Shadowed Under Eyes: He has some dark circles under his eyes which immediately give away that he is a deranged sinister murderer. Even Evil Has Standards: Played for laughs when the serial killer refuses to be overpaid for the drums, insisting that he's a killer, not a thief (even though he pays for them using the wallets of the people he killed). Played straight when Jerry makes up an elaborate backstory about how he stages his kills and kills people on their birthdays, and even seemingly planned tokill his own daughter, which the serial killer finds so abhorrent that he calls the police on Jerry despite his own crimes. Heel–Face Door-Slam: The serial killer was moved by Morty's words who connects with him on the fact that they both can't empathize with other people and are lashing out at the world because of that. The serial killer decides to drop his weapon and comes out unarmed, surrendering and wanting a hug. However, the Police immediately open fire and reduce him to ground meat on the spot.

characters.name: Shleemypants and Blip Blop
characters.description: A pair of omniscient, immortal and quite sassy time cops. All There in the Manual: Although his name is never brought up in the aired episode, anearly animaticshows Shleemypants introducing himself as such, along with him calling his fellow time cop "Blip Blop" via the phone. Been There, Shaped History: They try to go back to beat up Rick, but mistake Albert Einstein for him and proceed to beat the shit out of him while yelling at him to not break time. Einstein gets up while mumbling that hewillbreak time, and creates the theory of relativity. The Cameo: Appears in midseason finale of season 4 tobeat up the ancestor of a snake who discovers time travel. Complete Immortality: It's implied that not only is he immortal, but unkillable as well. However, this does not mean he can't be beaten into submission and/or unconsciousness just that it won't kill him outright.

characters.name: Story Lord
characters.description: The man at the helm of the Story Train. He is trying to drain Rick and Morty's supposedly infinite storytelling potential. As of "Full Meta Jackrick" he's escaped to the real world. Allegorical Character: In a meta sense, he is twofold. One is of network executives that want to turnRick and Mortyinto ainvokedCash-Cow Franchise, and the other is something of aTake That!towards fans who wantRick and Mortyto be some serialized epic story. There are, however, also clear elements of aSelf-DeprecatingAuthor Avatarof show co-creatorDan Harmonin him, especially in how his scheme is modelled after Harmon's famous story-circle model. Author Avatar: He looks like a buff Dan Harmon. In his second appearance, he turns out to be a recursive example: being the author avatar of a character who is also an avatar of Dan Harmon. Bad Boss: He uses Previous Leon as bait to lure Rick and Morty into meta reality then has Jesus rip Leon's wings off for no reason. He then abandons Jesus himself once he can escape the fourth wall himself and goes on to use his creator as slave labor to empower himself. Beard of Evil: He's a villain with a chinstrap beard.

characters.name: Jesus Christ
characters.description: Jesuswas initially summoned by a fictional Rick and Morty in a literalDeus ex Machinain "Never Ricking Morty". He reappears in "Full Meta Jackrick after he gets summoned by Previous Leon and then the Story Lord. Ambiguous Situation: Is he the literal Jesus Christ or something resembling humanity's interpretation of Jesus? "The Last Temptation Of Jerry" confirms that the Easter holidays were formed around an alien who visited the Middle-East over 2000 years ago, with at least one other member of his species having the "Jesus look", albeit with green skin. Deus ex Machina: A literal example. Story Lord, using his machine to extract the "unlimited storytelling potential" of Rick and Morty, shows them "the end of [their] story", where they are cornered by an enormous army led by Evil Morty. To thwart him, Rick and Morty deliberately invoke anOut-of-Character Momentandpray for salvationfrom... Jesus Christ, who literally descends from the heavens to save them. I Just Want to Be Normal: Immortal Jesus asks a witch and later god to make him normal. I Work Alone: Jesus rejects Napoleon's offer by telling him that he works alone.

characters.name: Scary Terry
characters.description: A monster found in the dreams of Morty's math teacher. To be specific, he was found in the dream of a centaur, who was in the dream of a T.V. character that Morty's math teacher was dreaming about. All-Ghouls School: He apparently went to school full of similarly scary students. Anti-Villain: He's only villainous because his race of people isexpectedto be, and at worst he's aPunch-Clock Villain. If he didn't have to scare people to survive as part of hisDream Walkerrace, he wouldn't have to be villainous. Captain Ersatz: He's an obviousFreddy Kruegerparody. Rick even calls him a "legally safe knock-off of an '80s horror villain." Dark Is Not Evil: He becomes this after Rick and Morty help him with his nightmares and is revealed to be an all aroundNice Guy, if not a little mean. The same can also be said about theDream Walkerrace that Scary Terry is a part of. Despite having knives for hands and full onFacial Horror, most of them are just ordinary people, but some can still be jerks or even friendly.

characters.name: Lucius Needful
characters.description: Summer's boss who also happens to be the Devil himself, operating a store where he gives people magical items at no cost. Predictably enough, the price is that said items usually screw over their new owners in ironic ways. The Devil Is a Loser: Rick continually makes a fool of him and evendrives him to try and hang himself. When Summer saves him, he admits that he just wants to go back to hell where people actually think his antics are cool and funny, unlike his experience on Earth. At the end of the episode, Needful gets beat up by a roided-out Rick and Summer. Even the Devil Is Shocked: The Devil, who nearly committed suicide due to Rick's atrocities, openly admits to Summer that Rick is much darker than he is.People like Rick are making me obsolete. I mean, seriously. I may be "The Devil", but your grandpa is THE Devil. Expy:Of Leland Gaunt fromNeedful Things, specifically the movie version, where Gaunt was the Devil in disguise.His design, however, is more based on Mr. Dark from the Disney adaptation of Ray Bradbury'sSomething Wicked This Way Comes. Of Leland Gaunt fromNeedful Things, specifically the movie version, where Gaunt was the Devil in disguise.

characters.name: Fart
characters.description: A telepathic, gaseous life form who was the target of Krombopulos Michael before Morty saves him. Affably Evil: Fart remains polite and thankful towards Morty for saving his life, despite his plans on killing him and his home planet. The only time he drops it was when he was revealing his plan to Morty, but picks it back up when Morty asks him to sing for him. Justified in that Fart genuinely believes that Morty understands and agrees with him. Anti-Villain: Of the moreObliviously Evilkind. He genuinely believes in his cause and harbors no grudge towards his rescuers other than that they are carbon-based. Right up to the reveal, he helps Rick and Morty and remains cooperative. And whenThe Revealhits, he believes that there is nothing wrong with his intentions, and believes that Morty agrees. He reacts with shock and horror as Morty kills him, not understanding why. Appropriated Appellation: Rick mocks him as a "mind-reading fart". Despite Morty's protests, the cloud decides that he likes being called Fart and decides that it's his new name. Drama-Preserving Handicap: His gaseous form means he can't survive going through one of Rick's portals, so Rick and Morty have to transport him to the wormhole the long way, resulting in Fart slowly revealing to Morty his true nature.

characters.name: The Cromulons
characters.description: A race of planet-sized, planet-stealing floating faces. They abduct planets for their version of a musical reality show, and blow the losing planets to smithereens. Blue-and-Orange Morality: As planetary sized beings, they have a very different understanding of morality to that of humans. Earth-Shattering Kaboom: They invoke this on planets if they're disqualified from their show. Karma Houdini: They've destroyed many inhabited planets in the name of their own entertainment and receive no comeuppance in the end. Lack of Empathy: They kidnap entire planets for the sake of agame show. And if they don't comply, well, then their planet gets disqualified.Explosively so.

characters.name: Tickets Please Guy
characters.description: The conductor(?) on the Story Train. Is suprisingly ripped for an old man. And I Must Scream: Due to how he ends up getting trapped between the inside and the outside of the train, hisCruel and Unusual Deathis drawn out formonthsfrom his own perspective. Cruel and Unusual Death: He is sucked out a window into space, ripped in half in the process, then because of the effects of the train, he experiences a months-long hell of spinning in a circle spraying blood everywhere before Morty finally puts him out of his misery.

characters.name: Ricklets
characters.description: Literally Shattered Lives: What happens to them after they are literally erupted from the ground by Gaia giving birth, which means significant outside intervention is required for them to even live. Revenge: Beth is concerned that Gaia will raise them to hunt down the Smith family for Zeus' death. Rick assures her that he put a tracking device on their ship and he'll blow it up if they try. Semi-Divine: Half living planet, half god. Silicon-Based Life: They are sentient clay humanoids that slightly resemble Rick. Strong Family Resemblance: At first it seems like they're Rick's kids because they seemingly inherit his pointy hair. Turns out they get their hair from their real father.

characters.name: Reggie
characters.description: A Zeus-like god who is the real father of Gaia's children. Cruel and Unusual Death: A ship being driven by a high Morty and Summer gets lodged in his skull, then Rick pilots it out his eye socket. This results in his cloud form breaking down and his body getting impaled on the tower of Rick's city. Cumulonemesis: How he appears at first, but this is justa form he takes to appeal more to Gaia. Jerkass Gods: He's got powers on par with Zeus, and he's not interested in anything to do with his children except teach them fear. A Kind of One: He's not Zeus. He'sazeus. There are probably other zeuses elsewhere.

characters.name: Demons
characters.description: Demons that feed on suffering that Rick tried to con. As payback, they force him to accompany them on "guys night" and inflict the worst possible torture they know on him: including Jerry. Bad Is Good and Good Is Bad: Parodied to hell and back. The demons rarely let a minute go by without reminding whoever they're speaking to that whatever regular people find bad, the demons find pleasurable. A bad day is really a good day, a cry for help is actually a cry not to be helped, even the demons feeling insulted or embarrassed only leads to them feeding off of their own misery and converting it back into pleasure. Cringe Comedy: The real reason they take Jerry with them on guys night is feeding off of the cringe he induces in Rick. Since Jerry's too oblivious to feel embarrassed about the way he acts, they feed off of Rick's annoyance with his son-in-law's "lameness" and plan on imprisoning them both in hell just to feed off it forever. Deal with the Devil: The demons made one with Rick and ended up with faulty skin hooks. Then they made another one for payback where Rick had to go on "guys nights" with them, and bring Jerry along. Emotion Eater: They feed off of the physical and emotional suffering of anyone, including themselves. Any shame or sadness they feel only makes them feel pleasure.

characters.name: The Meteors
characters.description: According to Rick, "barely" sentient meteors evolved along with the dinosaurs to have become just as selflessly evil as the dinosaurs become selflessly good. Thereby, they are currently rocks of pure rage with the singular intent to destroy any utopia created by the dinosaurs. Always Chaotic Evil: The sentient meteors, who only appear to live to destroy planets improved upon by the Dinosaurs and speak only inAngrish. Angrish: The living meteor spouts nothing but incomprehensible rage-speak and angry screaming. Balance of Good and Evil: The show gives aScience Fictionversion of the concept with the dinosaurs and the sentient meteors. While the dinosaurs evolved into "higher and higher levels of loving vegan godhood, another life-form devolved into an equally selfless hate-filled species of barely-sentient rocks" that seek out the dinosaurs as a form ofAnimal Jingoism, crashing into every planet that the dinosaurs colonize. Fake Ultimate Mook: While they resembled terrifying and unstoppable threats to the dinosaurs, it turned that the dinosaurscould in fact kill them. It's just that they were so pacifistic they couldn't bring themselves to kill another life-form.

characters.name: Knights of the Sun
characters.description: An order of Knights who live on the sun and protect the Solar System. Human Aliens: The Knights of the Sun, apart from the immortality granted by their station,have fused carbon walls for blood vesselsmaking them immune to overdosing on heroin. Jerkass Has a Point: One of the Knights reminds everyone that Morty refused to follow their ways and unwittingly disillusioned their beliefs. So why bother following their "king's" command to reunite if he doesn't change his mind? Living Forever Is Awesome: The Knights of the Sun declare that they have the good kind of immortality you don't get bored with and can die whenever you want. Also, living on the sun means they can't overdose from heroin. Unfortunately, part of the initiation ritual is cutting off your dick, and that's a deal-breaker for Morty. Poor Communication Kills: Over and over and over the Knights of the Sun boof it. They fail to explain that it's a kind of ritualYou Kill It, You Bought Itsituation with becoming a knight, then fail to explain that you have to cut your dick off to join, then spring that you have to beat the king in combat in order to leave, only for that to turn out to beanotherYou Kill It, You Bought It, and then it turns out that they've all been incredibly stupid about their religion and thought the solar system literally orbited the scepter when really it was a political metaphor.

characters.name: Noble Houses of the Solar System
characters.description: Representatives of various planets. Added Alliterative Appeal: Their royal titles coincide with the planets they represent (Viscount of Venus, Marquis of Mars, Earl of Earth etc.). Chromatic Arrangement:Mercury is blueVenus is blackEarth is redMars is orangeSaturn is greenJupiter is purple Looks Like Cesare: The Viscount of Venus is a thin man with pale skin and long black hair. His people all share his appearance. Remember the New Guy?: Rick explains that the reason him and Morty never encountered these guys before is because they did not exist in the previous universes the family inhabited. Seems they are localised entirely in the "parmesian" universe.

characters.description: Omniescent alien stones that record all of history. Asshole Victim: Morty accidentally killing the first Observer by kicking him into a truck. Overboard? Perhaps. Satisfying nonetheless? Definitely. Can't Take Criticism:The first Observer overpowers Rick and Morty's settlement to show off its powers, leading the two to protest that he seems more interested in presenting aClip Showand rudely pay him to leave. Insulted, the Observer harasses the Smith family with humiliating clips outside their house.Morty:Just take the L. This is embarrassing!Observer:I'll showyouembarrassing.(cuts to another clip)The Observer court don't prove much better. When Rick turns the tables on them by revealing all of their dirty laundry, they quickly resort to deflecting onto each other and eventually devolve into a riot. characters.name: The Fear Hole
characters.description: An open sewer crack located in a local Denny's bathroom stall that forces anyone who enters it to confront and overcome their worst fear. Affably Evil: Feeds on terror and despair, and will insult those who challenge it when sufficiently miffed, but it makes good on its promise on helping entrants deal with their worst fears. On its intro video tape, its Avatar is even seen cheerfully helping a patron of the Fear Hole out of the hole itself. And is very upfront about the experience and why it promotes it. Ambiguously Evil: The Hole's avatar is quite sinister and it's quite ruthless about scaring people, but it's left ambiguous how evil it actually is. It's possible the Hole - as it says in the VHS tape - harmlessly feeds off of fear and helps people conquer it. Yet it also claims it wants to feed off its victims' fear until they die, and Rick and Morty are gradually drained of their energy while they stay inside the Hole. Yet this too could simply be it trying to scare its customers into overcoming their fears, which is supported by the fact the Fear Hole ends Morty's vision once he realizes what his true fear was. Ambiguous Situation:The Revealcasts a long shadow overanythingit says and/or that happens after Morty enters The Hole. Was Morty at any risk of dying, or was that just a way to raise the stakes? Was "Diane" an accurate recreation of the real thing, or was she just based on Morty's assumptions? We will likely never know. Animal Motif: Its avatar likens the Hole to a red garra or "doctor/nibble fish" due to the purportedly benign symbiotic relationship it has with its entrants while it feeds.

characters.name: The Collective
characters.description: A being from beyond the Central Finite Curve who absorbed universes into themselves. The Assimilator: The threat Evil Morty extorts Rick into helping him fight is a being called The Collective, which assimilates entire universes into itself, threatening the Central Finite Curve. They eventually defeat it by studying a sample and developing an algorithm that,when assimilated, forces the Collective to absorb itself, causing all of its matter to rip off everything it assimilated and collapse into a thumb drive. Disc-One Final Boss: Gets defeated by Rick and Evil Morty at the end of the episode's first act, allowing Evil Morty to take over as the main antagonist in time for theFinal Battlein the episode's third act. Foil: The Collective is what Unity could be if they decided to stop respecting boundaries for some planets. Also, MUCH more efficient in absorbing others as it absorbs "all" while Unity just assimilates living beings. Purple Is Impure: The Collective as well as everything and everyone it corrupts is purple.

characters.name: IT Cloud Entity
characters.description: A gaseous life form that performs customer service at Huge Clouds Metallurgy. Good Counterpart: The Tech Support/IT Cloud Entity that Rick calls in to unlock his garage acts as one of these to both Fart from "Mortynight Run" (another gaseous, non-organic cloud-like lifeform that Rick and Morty previously teamed up with) and the Observer from "Rickfending Your Mort" (also an inorganic life form that Rick called for help with a conflict Morty started).The Cloud Entity looks a lot like Fart and is capable of entering the minds of organic beings just like him, also briefly possessing someone for the sake of killing a whole bunch of people to help Rick and Morty. But where Fart caused the object of his possession to beDriven to Suicideand killed numerous cops, which was not Morty's plan, the Cloud Entity possesses one of the antagonists ofLa Résistance(who are actively trying to murder the Smiths) to kill the rest of them, which certainlyisRick's intention. And while Fart was outright genocidal against organic, carbon-based lifeforms, the Cloud Entityloveshaving a body made of physical matter when it possesses Jerry, has no ill intentions for him or the rest of the Smiths, and in fact outright helps the family during the fight and enjoys getting to know them.The Observer was aBitch in Sheep's Clothingwho pretty quickly went rogue and started doing his own thing not too long after Rick hired him, especially once Rick and Morty (and then the rest of the family) got sick of his shit and started being outright rude to him. While it initially looks like the Cloud Entity is going rogue with Jerry's body by taking it out for a joyride against Rick's orders, it's aSheep in Sheep's Clothingwho does come back once it's had its fun and unlocks the garage for him as it was hired to do, and then sticks with the Smiths during the house fight.Tellingly, unlike the other two, the Cloud Entity not only survives the episode, it gets a pretty happy ending. characters.name: Vance Maximus, Renegade Star Soldier
characters.description: A renegade Star Soldier who's the charismatic face of the Vindicators. The Ace: Vance Maximus, Renegade Star Soldier. Handsome? Check. Cool voice? Check. Cool outfit? Check. Slick personality? Check. Awesome name? Check. Ultimately subverted, ashe not only turns out to be aDirty Cowarddeep down, but is also the first to die, at the hands of an avoidable death. Black-and-White Insanity:What his speech in Vindicators 2 really consists of, as he insists to his teammates that as long as they are perceived as heroes to the public, anyone they harm or kill will be the “bad guy” of the story by default. Given his true nature, it’s very likely that he either genuinely believes this or is simply fine lying to and deluding the rest of his team into thinking they’re the good guys so he can get away with doing anything he wants. Captain Ersatz: Vance Maximus is similar to Peter Quill, aka Star-Lord, in that they both wear cool jackets, use jetpacks and have cool personalities. HisMr. Vice Guyantics are also similar toIron Man. Cruel and Unusual Death:Vance panics and flies into a trap in the ceiling. The upper half of his body isslowlygrinded into bits. The lower half flies all over the place before Crocubot blows it up.

characters.name: Alan Rails
characters.description: A man who gained the power to summon ghost trains after his parents tragically died in a railroad accident. He's Supernova's ex-husband. Broken Pedestal:It’s implied in the prequel Vindicators 2 shorts that he’s grown to have this opinion of his team, from having to help cover up his then-wife’s murders of a few of their teammates plus an entire bar AND a planet, and is wracked with guilt over those actions. Come Vindicators 3, he doesn’t seem to view any of his teammates with as much high regard anymore, especially his ex Supernova and 1 Million Ants (who had an affair with each other while Alan and Supernova were married). Captain Ersatz: Alan Rails is more similar to heroes like theGreen LanternandGhost Riderin terms of powers, but he has a sad backstory, much likeDrax the Destroyer. Catchphrase: "All aboard!" Cock Fight:Alan Rails and 1-Million Ants fight because 1-Million Ants had sex with Supernova, Alan's ex-wife but current wife during the affair. When Alan was justifiably pissed off about the affair and had tried to attack 1-Million Ants, both are restrained by Supernova but 1-Million Ants took advantage of this and killed Alan by force-feeding him until he exploded.

characters.name: 1 Million Ants
characters.description: A colony comprised of a million sentient red ants. Ambiguous Gender Identity: 1-Million Ants is unsure whether to identify with the female queen, the male drones that comprise the body or the genderless collective. After trying to decide on a pronoun for an online dating profile, 1-Million Ants gets overwhelmed and gives up. Captain Ersatz: 1-Million Ants is similar to Groot in that he's a non-human humanoid creature with extra-human powers. He's also a literalAnt-Man. Captain Obvious: 1-Million Ants uses his psychic powers to point out the blindingly obvious, to the point where Rick says he has the superpowers of a person with two eyes. Cock Fight:Alan Rails and 1-Million Ants fight because Million Ants had sex with Supernova, Alan's ex-wife but current wife during the affair. When Alan was justifiably pissed off about the affair and had tried to attack Million Ants, both are restrained by Supernova but Million Ants took advantage of this and killed Alan by force feeding him until he exploded.

characters.name: Crocubot
characters.description: Captain Ersatz: Crocubot is similar toRocket Raccoonas a hyperintelligent cybernetically enhanced animal. He doesn't have any of Rocket's angst, though. Physically, he's a mix ofCyborgandKiller Croc. Cruel and Unusual Death:Crocubot is crushed between the floors beneath him when he gets a question wrong. Compared to the other deaths on this list, his was the fastest and least painful. Cyborg: Crocubot, half cold unfeeling machine and half cold unfeeling reptile. Ironically, he actually seems like one of the nicer ones. Emotionless Reptile: Crocubot is an alien who is half cold, unfeeling reptile and half cold, unfeeling machine. Rick points out that his existence is a living redundancy as crocodiles and robots are already cold and unfeeling independently. Hidden Depths: The Vindicators 2 shorts have one episode dedicated to showing Crocubot going off to a distant planet so he could dance in solitude, which he seems to genuinely enjoy.

characters.name: Noob-noob
characters.description: The Vindicators' intern who they use more as a janitor. Butt-Monkey: Practically nothing good happens to him at all throughout the episode. Catchphrase: "Goddamn!" Disproportionate Reward:Drunk Rick decided to spare Noob-Noob at the end because the latter laughed at his jokes in the briefing room. Ensemble Dark Horse:In-Universe, as Rick likes Noob-Noob more so than the others combined because Noob-Noob was the only one that was laughing at Rick's jokes.Even the finalSawtrap was actually made with Noob-Noob in mind, who didn't come onto the mission in order to clean up Rick's literal shit.

characters.name: Previous Members
characters.description: Three members of the Vindicators who were said to have died fighting Doom-Nomitron. Lady Katana was a cyborg who wielded katanas, Calypso was a sorceress, and Diablo Verde was a green demon. Absurdly Sharp Blade: Subverted; Lady Katana's swords are just regular swords rather than "Extra-Strength Swords", meaning that they can't cut through anything harder than steel. All Women Are Lustful: Downplayed, but Lady Katana seems to have a rather dirty sense of humor. Big Red Devil: Diablo Verde is a big green devil. Black Dude Dies First:Spoofed. During the off-screen "Vindicators 2", 3 members died:''Lady Katana'', ''Calypso'', and ''Diablo Verde''. Rick lampshades this.Rick: Yikes. Yeah, things did feel less diverse in there.

characters.name: Mr. Nimbus
characters.description: The ruler of the Ocean and Rick's self-declared nemesis. Arch-Enemy: He introduces himself as Rick's and Rick, despite not being the type of person to put any stock in the enemies he's made, begrudgingly and shamefully admits that Mr. Nimbus reallyishis nemesis. Beware the Silly Ones: While he's a half-naked weirdo who's constantly gyrating and shouting his name, he's enough of a threat that Rick feels the need to placate him. Big Damn Heroes: He saves Rick, Morty and Jessica from the futuristic Hoovians. Broken Pedestal: Nimbus and Rick actually used to be friends before they were enemies, but upon seeing how low Rick's fallen even after their rivalry, Nimbus gives a brief"The Reason You Suck" Speechthat actually manages to affect Rick."I used to fear you. Respect you! Now all that's left is pity for a sad, drunk shell of a man too afraid to see how alone he truly is."

characters.name: Concerto
characters.description: A mysterious musical-themed villain. Beware the Silly Ones: A joke villain who gets killed off almost instantly, and nevertheless had Rick terrified. Bright Is Not Good: Has a colorful appearance, but is a psychopath who kills people with a giant piano. Expy: His abnormally large grin and pale face are evocative of the Joker, and his giant piano-themedDeath Trapis reminiscent of a campy Batman villain. Flat Character: We never get to know about his motivations since he only appears inThe Stingerof "Pickle Rick", and gets his throat slit by Jaguar in aBig Damn Heroesmoment.

characters.name: Worldender
characters.description: The arch-enemy of the Vindicators and a galaxy-spanning terror. Bait-and-Switch: On a production level,the Adult Swim promo for this episodemakes the plot look like a standardSuper Teamstory with Worldender as the main villain, calling him "the most fearsome villain of the Rick and Morty multiverse" and "imagine Thanos fucked Darkseid and had a baby." Mid-episode, however, Worldender is killed by a drunken Rick the night before he returns with Morty and the Vindicators. Expy: The Worldender is what, as the staff noted, "if Thanos fucked Darkseid and, like, had a baby, and that baby then fucked some other giant creature monster, that's Worldender". Like Darkseid, he's a hulkingand fearedOmnicidal Maniacwho has conquered and destroyed many worlds. When his minions are found dead, the Vindicators assume he has Darkseid's tendencyto kill his own minions for petty reasons... Turns out that he and his minions were killed by a drunken Rick just to show the Vindicators up. Five-Second Foreshadowing: Just before the reveal that Rick has already killed Worldender and set up aSaw-style game for the Vindicators, we see that the corpses of Worldender's henchmen have been placed in sexually explicit poses with their pants off. That's not something a being like the Worldender would do, but it'sentirelysomething that a blackout drunk Rick Sanchez would do. Generic Doomsday Villain: Possibly the most blatant example you can imagine. It's never explained why Worldender causes Armageddon on various planets and he's killed offscreen before he himself can give any insight. When he appears in the Oni comicbooks, he's little more than aFeral Villain.

characters.name: The Tina-Teers
characters.description: Planetina's "kids," by which she means the four now middle-aged individuals with magic rings who summon her into existence. Asshole Victim: They're a bunch of greedy jerks who only see Planetina as a product to exploit, to the point where they're literally planning on selling her. Eddie is particularly odious, using his fire ring in an attempt to mutilate and/or murder Morty for dating Planetina. All of them get suitably painful deaths. Despite viewing them as her "kids", Planetina isn't terribly upset when Morty murders them all, instead feeling happy about her newfound freedom. Corrupt Corporate Executive: Once they grew into adults exploiting Planetina for money. Corrupted Character Copy: The Tina-teers are corrupt, middle-aged versions of the Planeteers, implied to have long since lost whatever idealism they once held in their youth, and now more concerned with filling their pockets than saving the planet and planning on selling Planetina to a shady man. Noticeably, the Tina-teers don't have a Heart counterpart. Decapitation Presentation: As part of Morty'sDelivery Guy Infiltrationto crash the Tina-Teers' sale of Planetina, he pretends to be a pizza man with a "cheesy Italian, extra crispy." Then he tosses Eddie's charred skull onto the table with the Water ring bearer recognizing Eddie's cheekbones.

characters.name: Diesel Weasel
characters.description: Planetina's archenemy. Captain Ersatz: Of Captain Planet's enemy Verminous Skumm. Corrupted Character Copy: He resembles one of theBiker Mice from Mars, but he's a villain rather than an edgy hero. For the Evulz: In his only scene he creates a cloud of acid rain for no reason. Plot-Irrelevant Villain: Diesel Weasel doesn't participate in any of the episode's conflicts, being little more than a reason to introduce Planetina.

characters.name: GoTronPilots
characters.description: A quintet of anime characters who pilot ferret-themed mechs that combine into a larger mech. Animesque: TheGoTronpilots play this straight, fromBig Anime Eyesto anime-style expressions. They try to reclaim the robot ferrets from Rick near to end of the episode since, as Kendra lampshades, they areliterallydesigned for the role of their pilots. Big Anime Eyes: Kendra has these. Lampshaded by Morty when he describes her to his family. Bilingual Bonus: The "GoTrons" are made up of five smaller mechs (originally driven by the five members of the Smith-Sanchez family) that assemble together to make a larger one. "Go" means "five" in Japanese. Celebrity Paradox: An earlier episode had an explicitVoltronreference, making theIn-Universeexistence of theGoTronsthis.

characters.name: Crowscare
characters.description: Rick's archenemy during his brief stint as a crow-themed superhero. Captain Ersatz: Of the Marvel version ofScarecrow, who originally used trained crows to commit crimes. Green and Mean: His outfit is mostly green in the grand tradition of supervillains. The interior of his base also has a green filter to make his presence more unsettling. Legion of Doom: The anime intro shows Crowscare's allies include anthropomorphic beasts like owl people, a tiger-man, a hawkman and a golem made of quartz. Scary Scarecrows: The anime intro shows Crowscare turning into a towering demon with fire breath. Even his default form is quite sinister, as it's not clear if he's wearing a mask or is in fact an animate scarecrow.

characters.name: Previous Leon
characters.description: A parasitic fly-like creature that crosses paths with Rick and Morty. Brought to You by the Letter "S": He wears a jacket with his initials on it. Healing Factor: He is able to grow his wings back after they get torn off of him by Jesus Christby feeding on his "potential" (read: life force). Lotus-Eater Machine: Previous Leon puts his victims in a fakePreviously on…segment while he drains them of their life force. Made of Iron: He suffers a lot of abuse throughout this episode, but shrugs them off with ease.

characters.name: The Self-Referential Six
characters.description: A group of metafiction-themed super beings. Ascended Extra: Protago-Nick can fire a beam that can make anyone the protagonist, even an extra. Ass Pull: Mr. Twist's power is this, being able to alter reality however he pleases as long as it's in the form of a plot twist, even if it came out of nowhere. Backstory Invader: Downplayed with Flash Back. While he doesn't meddle with people's backstories, he can take a peek at their past by suddenly appearing in a flashback. Bait-and-Switch: Miss Lead's introduction naturally involves giving Rick a greeting like they're old acquaintances, before haughtily slapping him.

characters.name: Rhett Caan
characters.description: A prisoner of the Self-Referential Six, with meta powers of his own. Even More Omnipotent: While Mr. Twist and ConnieTinuityErrorhaveReality Warperpowers, Rhett Caan is regarded as the strongest member of the team and effortlessly takes them out. Expy: Both his appearance and his godlike power are heavily based onDoctor Manhattan.
