Kryptonite Factor: According to Rick, Rhett Caan was imprisoned in a cell made out ofsportssince sports is the opposite of story and his powers affect storytelling. Meaningful Rename: He was formerly called Brett Caan, but changed his name to Rhett after hearing Morty wonder why that wasn't his name already since Rhett is a name too.

characters.name: Cookie Magneto
characters.description: A cookie-themed supervillain who challenges Rick and Morty to a fight. Bullying a Dragon: He chose to start a fight with Rick Sanchez. Expy: A tongue in cheek blatant copy ofMagneto, but for cookies. Heart Is an Awesome Power: Discussed. Morty asks if he can control cookie ingredients, pointing out that sugar is in so many things that this villain could theoretically control most physical matter. Mathematician's Answer: Morty asks him if he controls things people generally agree are cookies, he answers that what people call cookies are things he controls.

characters.name: Mr. Calypso
characters.description: A mischief-making imp that tries to become Rick's arch-enemy. Big, Stupid Doodoo-Head: He tries to provoke Rick by calling him an "ugly, drunk, ugly piece of shit". Rick is far too secure to take that personally, but he captures and kills Calypso anyway. Great Gazoo: He's a blatant expy of Superman's enemy Mr. Mxyzptlk. We Hardly Knew Ye: Rick kills him during a session with Dr. Wong.

characters.name: Piss Master
characters.description: A urine-themed supervillain who has it out for Rick. After Piss Master gets humiliated in a fight with Jerry Smith, he ends uptaking his own life. Rick takes pity on him and after learning he has a daughter worried about Piss Master, Rick decides to impersonate him so the world would remembed him as a hero. Abnormal Ammo: He whole gimmick is that his suit shoots weaponized piss. Alien Blood: His blood is purple. Boisterous Weakling: He makes a big deal out of his demands for Rick to fight him, but his combat skills are so meager that Jerry, of all people, is able to get the best of him. Came Back Wrong: Rick tries to revive him, but due to lack of oxygen circulation, his brain was already too damaged to properly function, leaving him a jabbering husk that Rick has to re-kill.

characters.name: Galactic Orbship
characters.description: An intergalactic conglomerate of guardians whose power source are mystical orbs. They conscript Jerry into their ranks after he fought Pissmaster. Artifact of Hope: Orbs are given to people who are seen by the Galactic Orbship as heroic, though their criteria of heroism seems to be based around popularity on social media. The orb secretes a mucus when the person holding it is pure of heart, and it generates enough power to run planet-busting weaponry like Jerry's suit. Captain Ersatz: ToThe Green Lanterncorps. They preside over the galaxy and bestow powerful weapons onto worthy individuals. Among their council are members that resemble a typical Oan guardian and a one-eyed Kilowog. Unlike their inspirations, however, the Orbship’s method of selection is less altruistic than it appears as it’s shown they select candidates based off of their popularity rank. Conflict Ball: The guardians order Jerry to deliver an orb to the reformed Piss Master despite their history. Jerry is given the option not to accept (and indeed many other candidates are shown unwilling to join), but he is told in no uncertain terms that he will be expelled if Piss Master doesn't take the orb, not even accounting for the fact he might have refused it. This ends up pushing Jerry into a situation that causes him to lose his orb and status.

characters.name: Legion of Hitlers
characters.description: A council of Hitler-themed supervillains from various planets and dimensions. Asshole Victim: Jerry blows up their entire planet without meaning to. Given everyone on the planet was some kind of Hitler, nobody judges Jerry. Captain Ersatz: Among the Hitler Legion are aRiddler-Hitlerand aGorilla Grodd Hitler. Given their entire planet is run by Hitler analogs, it can be compared toplanet Apokolips.

characters.name: Apeborg
characters.description: A supervillain that Rick and Morty faced at some point. Even Evil Has Standards: Apeborg is just as disgusted as Morty is when Rick gets the latter to French-kiss Apeborg in his nostrils. Expy: He resembles the albino gorilla-form of Superman's enemy Ultra-Humanite.

characters.name: Velocitrees
characters.description: A team of robots based on plants in a long-running film franchise. Accidental Murder: Due to Rick hating both Baron Thistle and Tannenbaum, he uses the Movie-Lizer to suddenly give Tannenbaum a gun who then shoots Baron Thistle's head off and has him sent to prison for manslaughter. As You Know: Rick gets annoyed at a scene where Tannenbaum conspicuously introduces the other Velocitrees by name, even though this is theninthfilm so everyone should know damn well who everyone is by now, and during the climax of the film on top of that. Autobots, Rock Out!: TheVelocitreestheme song is a reworked version of "One Week" byBarenaked Ladies, as a play on how James Gunn's movies tend to make heavy use of popular music. For added laughs, the song blatantly admits the franchise is brainless entertainment designed only to sell content. Chromatic Arrangement: They're all color-coded in the vein of the Power Rangers and other kid-friendly hero teams. This even extends to their arch-enemy, who wears a black coat.

characters.name: Baron Thistle
characters.description: TheBig Badfor theMaximum Velocitreefilm franchise. Bad Boss: As Morty discovers, Baron Thistle treated his henchmen quite poorly, as even a simple "thankyou" was enough to brighten their day. Cactus Person: The Baron looks human save for his skin being green and prickly. Came Back Wrong: When Rick and Morty tried to revive Baron Thistle with a bolt of lightning, they expected him to come back as his former self. Instead, he is a mindless zombie that attacks Morty on sight and has to be put down by Rick. Dark Is Evil: He wears a black coat, because he's the bad guy.

characters.name: President Andre Curtis
characters.description: Thedeeply immatureyetextremely badassPresident of the United States. He and Rick have a complicated relationship that swings between "friendly acquaintances" and "bitter rivals" largely depending on the current mood of both parties. He would later become the star of his ownself-titled seriesfocusing on his own adventures. Abusive Parents:Implied. In "Ricktional Mortpoon's Rickmas Mortcation", he states that one of the reason he loved the first twoStar Warsmovies was that it made "having a bad father empowering". Comments in "Air Force Wong" imply his mother was emotionally abusive. Acrofatic: He's a bit on the paunchy side under his clothes but that doesn't stop him from kicking ass every week. Action Politician: Becomes one by the time of "The Rickchurian Mortydate", complete with greater physical durability, mastery of gadgets, and operating his ownPowered Armor, showing himself capable of holding his own in a fight against Rick. It's also revealed that his administration has somehow managed to reverse-engineer its own portal technology, which while not as strong as Rick's (point to point on the same planet, not multiversal) is perfectly functional.

characters.name: Rho Banks
characters.description: President Curtis's new Chief of Staff. A cybernetically enhanced lady, she's new to the White House, but with her technical prowess and strong sense of morals, will prove invaluable in the future. Action Girl: Downplayed. Banks isn’t a fighter like Curtis or a powerhouse like O’Doyle, with her generally leaving the actual action to them. However, when pushed into a corner, she is capable of throwing down and has survived a number of very dangerous situations; she’s just not particularly enthusiastic about it. Ambiguously Brown: Tanner than the Caucasian O'Doyle but lighter than Curtis, no hints to her ethnic background or culture have been dropped as of yet. Amnesiac Dissonance: Banks has no memory of her life before the operation that made her a cyborg.Thus, she’s horrified to discover her previous self was aMad Scientistparty animal, who experimented on multiple people to develop cyborg technology, leading to multiple deaths. She considers erasing her memory of this, but O’Doyle convinces her to embrace it, much the same way he has about his own miserable past. Audience Surrogate: As a new member of The White House, Banks is the lens through which we come to know the extent of presidential secrets and the supernatural threats that the team faces.

characters.name: Special Agent Francis O'Doyle
characters.description: The President's most trusted Secret Service agent. A half Leprechaun with great firearm and physical training, and a strong dedication to his boss. Abusive Parents: According to the other leprechauns, O'Doyle's mother was a piece of work. He once tried to practice doing the jig in the moorlands to impress her. However, when Orla found out, she made him dance for hours on end while all the other leprechauns mocked his dancing skills; it went on so long that by the end of it, Francis's feet were bloody. He also mentions she locked him in the trunk of a car she sold to a first-time driver and made him take a "scissor bath" for messing up the Clan's jig. She also tries toframe him for stealing Fort Knox's goldto box him in. All the Other Reindeer: Due to being half-leprechaun, he is mistrusted by most humans for being a potential supernatural criminal while mocked by other Leprechauns for being half-human. This naturally puts a huge chip on his shoulder. Anti-Hero: Very dedicated to the job of following presidential orders, but has no hard lines for himself in the process. He's even willing to torture an American citizen (in the CIA, but still) just because he was ordered to. Aura Vision: O'Doyle is capable of focusing his vision to track people, partially seeing through walls, the afterimages of their paths and a rainbow aura trailing behind them, as he can divine personal details about their history and emotional state, which he reflexively tells everyone even though it doesn't help.

characters.name: Janice
characters.description: The President's secretary. An older lady who's constantly passing messages and visitors to the President. Break-Up/Make-Up Scenario: Gets this with both Toomoo (romantically) and O'Doyle (platonically) during "Hollow". Janice bonds with O'Doyle while he's assigned to guard her after he gains respect for her badassery, but when he sees Toomoo with other women, O'Doyle assumes he's cheating on her and threatens him to stay away from her. Toomoo reluctantly does, causing Janice to think he's ghosting her for no reason and breaking her heart, and once O'Doyle casually reveals what happened, she's angry with him for meddling when she never cared to begin with if Toomoo hooked up with other women. O'Doyle eventually fixes his mistake by saving Toomoo from charging into battle and being killed, instead bringing him back to Janice so they can reconcile properly, which they do and for which she is grateful. December–December Romance: With Toomoo, herNew Old Flamefrom the Daaboo civilization, making it anInterspecies Romanceas well. Janice appears to be somewhere in her 70's or 80's, and Toomoo is old enough that he's considered the "village elder" of the Daaboo. Doting Grandparent: Possibly. She keeps pictures in her wallet of all 18 grandkids, which she offers to show O'Doyle, "starting with the uggos." Loyal to the Position: She's one of the Camp David "Lifers", who look down on white house staff tied to a particular president and individual presidents. That being said, she doesn't act rude like several of the other Lifers do and is pretty consistently friendly to the main cast, and for the time that Curtis is in office, she's got his back.

characters.name: Special Agent Alan Chomps
characters.description: Another agent of the Secret Service brought in when O'Doyle is reassigned to re-evaluation. The Ace: He's described by the head of Homeland Security as the highest-ranking agent of the Secret Service. Although he's not enthused about the President taking on supernatural threats himself, he's more than capable of helping him fight werewolves when they threaten his ex-wife's inauguration banquet, and is aNice Guywho lacks O'Doyle's many issues, making an effective agent. It's a bit of aRunning Gagthat everyoneelsethinks he's great, especially folks outside the White House, while thePower Triojust finds him annoying. Blessed with Suck: On paper, becoming a werewolf seems to offer multiple advantages, as it makes Chomps incredibly strong, fast, virtually invulnerable to anything other than silver, and is even implied to drastically enhance his lifespan, all without him losing his personality. However, adjusting to his new feral instincts proves to be very difficult, with him accidentally mauling an innocent bystander. Plus, his extended lifespan coupled with the agency’s policy on paranormal agents means that now his retirement (which he was looking forward to after his lengthy, taxing service) has been pushed back for another thirty-five years. Butt-Monkey: Chomps, simply put, has no luck. Despite being an exemplary agent, Curtis openly doesn’t like him much due to thinking he’s uncool. Months away from his retirement, he gets turned into a werewolf thanks toTaking the Bulletfor Curtis, which means he now has to work for another thirty-five years. His troubles adjusting mean he can’t join Curtis’s team, and due to an accident the first time he’s called into action as a werewolf, he ends up being dropped out of a plane to his death (though his werewolfHealing Factorthankfully allows him to revive from it). Curtis is at least a little nicer to him post-transformation, but Chomps still remainsThe Team Wannabeleft out of his inner circle. Boss's Unfavorite Employee: Due to

characters.name: Dr. Kenny Finch
characters.description: A scientist and inventor responsible for many of President Curtis’ technological needs and upgrades. Gadgeteer Genius: His role in the team is to effectively be the Q to Curtis’ James Bond, providing him with technological needs and gadgets, from his phones linked to various supernatural areas to Chomp’s special werewolf-management techno-collar. Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!: After Chomps wolfs out offscreen and chews a guy's legs off, Finch creates an add-on for his collar that will de-wolf him in the presence of innocent beings before he can attack them. However, when Chomps is being transported in a cage that keeps videos of meat constantly playing so he remains a wolf, Finch cheaping out by not paying for the ad-free video player means that an ad with a cute puppy starts playing at one point, activating the color's failsafe and turning Chomps back into human form at the worst possible time. No-Respect Guy: He's the most brilliant inventor seen across both series besides (some version of) Rick Sanchez himself, but it's aRunning Gagthat the President and his staff are constantly nitpicking his work and criticizing any little thing they don't like instead of praising him.Finch: You know, I'm getting a lot of notes for someone who got woken up at 3 AM and is still crushing it.

characters.name: Abraham Lincoln
characters.description: Yes,THAT Lincoln. After his death, he became trapped as a ghost in the Lincoln Bedroom. For his birthday, Curtis gives him "Ghost Gloves" that allow him to interact with the material world. Action Politician: When he finally goes mad, he's capable of kicking the ass of the Secret Service, helped by the fact that he's incorporeal save for his metal Ghost Gloves. Lincoln was a former professional boxer before he became a lawyer and politician, after all. Drunk with Power: Being given another chance to touch things after more than a century of being incorporeal soon goes to his head as he goes mad with power and decides to launch a missile at Virginia in an attempt to rekindle the Civil War. Dude, Where's My Respect?: Feels that his presidency is underappreciated just because he became most known for dying, and considers it an insult that his face was chosen to mint on a penny, a practically-worthless piece of currency that's no longer made. (He must not know about the $5 bill.) Slave Liberation:Played with. "The Rickturian Mortydate" has Curtis imply that Lincoln built a colosseum and kept some slaves to form an undergroundfightclub. This isn't mentioned when he appears in "Ghosts", though, so maybe this universe's version of Lincoln didn't do that.Curtis:He didn't free themall…

characters.name: Adam / Moon Baby
characters.description: Adam. A baby left on the moon by the CIA and Kennedy (allegedly), hoping to breed a new super president for the future. It...didn't go as planned. Bizarre Human Biology: He was modified to survive on the moon which includes extended lung capacity that goes all the way to his butt cheeks. The Caligula: While he never holds official position he believes he's inherited the office of President by birthright and thinks that his interests as such are the only ones that matter. Foil: his own inflated sense of importance contrasts with Curtis, as he uses the same phrase to justify his own desires. I'm a Humanitarian: Ate the other moon babies that were sent up to him.

characters.name: Amelia Earhart
characters.description: THEAmelia Earhart. Somehow, she became immortal and was found in the Bermuda Triangle during Franklin D Roosevelt's administration, causing her to become the primary means of transportation in that area. Ace Pilot: She's trusted to reliably fly through the very treacherous Bermuda Triangle. Ambiguously Human: She describes herself as "kind of a zombie, kind of a ghost" in regards to how she's still alive but hasn't physically aged. Historical Domain Character: She's the legendary female pilot who, as it turns out, has survived in the Bermuda Triangle in this universe. Redeeming Replacement: She ends up being appointed the new Warden of the Triangle followingWarden Jennings'sdeath. Unlike Jennings, who was a bigoted, corrupt, murderous man, Amelia is a lot more empathetic, pointing out that in her time, she was considered a "monster" as well just like the prisoners who are sent there, and focuses on trying to rehabilitate the inmates.

characters.name: Governor Beverly Mills
characters.description: The President's Ex Wife, and the Ex first lady of the nation. After the divorce, she decided to become Governor of Illinois, and became successful in ways few would've expected. Action Politician: She's just as much of an action hero as her ex. Amicable Exes: Despite some of the tension between the two, Beverly and Curtis generally keep up polite appearances for the public, and both care about each other despite all that happened between them. By the end of her introductory episode, they don't get back together because of their respective political careers, but part on good terms and don't completely close to the door to reconciliation in the future. Foil: She is this to her ex-husband President Curtis. Whereas Curtis is anAction Herowho prefers to beat down and arrest supernatural creatures through violence, She prefers to use diplomatic methods to rehabilitate supernatural creatures for the common good. This leads to them disagreeing over dealing with the werewolves when they attack her conference. They settle for the compromise of defeating and arresting them, since these ones explicitly cannot and do not want to be reformed, without killing any more of them. Never a Self-Made Woman:She goes out of her way to defy this trope HARD,making it quite clear that she is more than just the President's (Ex)-Wife and is an accomplished politician who has done great things on her own without President Curtis. Though this also forces her to keep her ex-husband at arm's length,knowing any misunderstanding could lead to a tabloid scandal that she'd rather not deal with.

characters.name: Salem Montgomery and his Vampire Coven
characters.description: Ambition Is Evil: Choosesto ally with the French for more territory to hunt. Even Evil Has Standards:Is a treacherous, bloodthirsty vampire. But even he seems a bit disturbed when he mistakenly believes that Curtis deliberately dropped one of his own men out of a helicopter to his death for no apparent reason. Immortality: They are vampires after all. They've been in America since at least the Louisiana Purchase and personally knew Jefferson. Must Be Invited: As Vampires, they cannot enter territories without a proper invitation.The reason they chose to betray the US is because Jefferson exploited this to ensure that they're stuck in Louisiana and they hope that by siding with the French they can broaden their feeding territory.

characters.name: Elsie
characters.description: Action Girl: More than capable of going toe to toe with the French andher vampire ex-coven-mates. When Elsie joins Team Curtis in fighting them, she has the highest kill count by far. Category Traitor: Turns against her vampire coven both because they didn't tell her the plan, and because she's disgusted with said plan once she does find out about it, which involves thembetraying an ally. Deadpan Snarker: Is more than able to diss back at O'Doyle for his lack of grace. Karmic Jackpot:Due to being the only vampire who doesn't betray the President and helps him win against the Frenchmen, she's one of the very few vampires who survives the episode, and O'Doyle specifically invites her to visit them in DC, allowing her to leave Louisiana.

characters.name: The Chicago Werewolf Syndicate
characters.description: A group of werewolf terrorists. Elite Mooks: Strictly speaking, the werewolves are a challenge for normal people to fight without silver. Thus, Curtis and Chomps end up struggling quite a bit with each one they face. Evil Reactionary: Has this feeling towards what's going on in the world. They disrespect all former monsters who aren't "living up to their potential" (read: reforming and getting actual jobs or benefiting society rather than continuing to just kill and terrorise people). Hence, their attack on Chicago. Fantastic Terrorists: A terrorist group that is entirely composed of werewolves. They hold the fundraiser attendees hostage with a bomb designed to fire werewolf teeth, threatening to infect them all if they don’t hand over a fortune for them to use for their cause.

characters.name: The Napoleonic Louisiana Acquisition Cell
characters.description: A group of Frenchmen raised in secret to retake The Louisiana Purchase as soon as America breaks the secret provision in the sale. After Curtis accidentally triggers a notice, they rise up to retake all 15 states for France. Catchphrase: Vive Napoleon! Brawn Hilda: The cell’s leader, Commodante Duloc, is a huge, brawny muscular woman. Dark Action Girl: The Cell has a number of female members in the present, most notably their leader, Commodante Duloc, who are just as dangerous as their male members. No Name Given: The only one named is their leader Commodante Duloc

characters.name: David
characters.description: The water witch of Camp David. Imprisoned since Franklin Roosevelt, she wants to get out and constantly challenges presidents for their "kingdoms". Gender-Blender Name: She's female, but is named "David", which is a masculine name. Immune to Bullets: Due to her water-based body, bullets just harmlessly pass straight through, and she immediately heals. O’Doyle acknowledges special rounds would be effective against her, but he didn’t bring any due to not knowing what sort of supernatural she was. Logical Weakness: David’s water-based body makes her immune to bullets, which just harmlessly pass through; however, larger physical weaponry like throwing Hatchets can at least delay her, as they physically stick into her body and she has to remove them before she can heal. Manipulative Bastard: All about trying to get "a king" to free her from a binding spell.

characters.name: Orfhlaith O'Doyle
characters.description: Francis O'Doyle's mother, the head of Clan O'Doyle and a leprechaun renowned for her cruelty and vile nature. Abusive Parents: She's both emotionally and physically abusive, having once forced a young Francis to do a jig until his feet bled, and several of his scars that he's since covered with tattoos came from her, directly or indirectly. Her first appearance in the present day sees her framing him as an accomplice to her robbery of Fort Knox. Naturally, her sondespisesher, and claiming otherwise is aBerserk Buttonfor him. Archnemesis Mom: It really is no wonder why O'Doyle hates his leprechaun ancestry considering how evil and abusive his mother is. Aura Vision: Just like her son, Orfhlaith can read people’s auras; however, her ability is so powerful she can do so through any material within a fifty-yard radius; it's mentioned she used it to casually drive two guards to insanity during her transfer to the FBI’s facility. Beware the Silly Ones: You'd assume a leprechaun wouldn't be capable of being a national threat, but not only do leprechaunspossess a wide variety of powers, Orfhlaith is nasty and diabolical even among her kind andeven being sent to the Triangle isn't a big deal for her.

characters.name: Principal Gene Vagina
characters.description: The principal of Morty and Summer's high school. A middle-aged, balding man with a shitty name that he constantly has to emphasize he has no relation to the female body part, Principal Vagina is a surprisingly level-headed person in such a messed up world. Dissonant Serenity: As stated in the description, he is very calm and brushes off stuff like hiring a vampire as a PE teacher as if it were an everyday thing. Drunk with Power: After establishing the Headism Religion. Embarrassing Last Name: But don't let that fool you, he's very much in charge. According to him, his best guess is that it's possibly Scandinavian. Mad Libs Catchphrase: He always introduces himself as "Principal Gene Vagina, the name's real ______"

characters.name: Mr. Goldenfold
characters.description: Morty and Summer's math teacher. Badass Teacher: Only in his dreams...and when rebelling against the Galactic Federation. Butt-Monkey: His existence is pretty sad both inandout of school. Characterization Marches On: Was presented as a typical angry black man in his first appearance. He is shown as much calmer whenever he appears after. A Day in the Limelight: "Rise of the Numbericons: The Movie" puts him in a role Rick usually occupies and deals with his history as Ice-T's former math teacher.

characters.name: Coach Feratu
characters.description: The Ghost: He's dealt with entirely offscreen. Our Vampires Are Different: This is the first time vampires have been mentioned in the show, although Rick seems to take them for granted. Steven Ulysses Perhero: His choice of name wasn't exactly subtle. Too Dumb to Live: His vampire master thinks as much when he hears what his assumed name was.

characters.name: Gordon Lunas
characters.description: A new guidance counsellor at Morty's high school. Dark Is Not Evil: Despite looking like a typical cartoon villain, he was revealed to have been a respected marine officer and aguidance counsellor. Driven to Suicide: He took his own life after being falsely accused of being a pedophile. Meaningful Name: His name is GordonLunasand he is accused of living on the Moon. Mentor Archetype: Invoked, but Ultimately subverted.Mr. Lunas:I look forward to helping guide you all towards a brighter future. I believe every student shouldshoot for the moon.

characters.name: Miss Underwood
characters.description: A teacher that the students bully. No-Respect Guy: Not only did a student draw a nasty picture of her, they also wrote a death threat on the back.

characters.name: Frank Palicky
characters.description: A bully who appeared in the pilot episode of the series. Frank Palicky carried a knife around in school and threatened to make anyone who called his family poor pay the price for doing so. He was summarily frozen by Rick, then toppled over and shattered on his own, killing him instantly. Asshole Victim: Downplayed, despite being anan absolute lunatic, Frank's death is shown to traumatize Summer and results in the school being on edge for the rest of the episode. Ax-Crazy: Becomes angry enough over just ten seconds to try to "cut" Morty with a switchblade, right in front of everyone else in the hallway. Berserk Button: Don't call his family poor. Or say anything that might make him think you called his family poor. Or... it's probably best if you don't talk at all around him, actually. The Bully: His almost-instant death upon introduction was meant to parody the concept by immediately having him turn out to be irrelevant to the series as a whole.

characters.name: Ethan B.
characters.description: Summer's boyfriend, who's shown to be extremely clingy and dealing with his own insecurities. His body becomes the building site for the new Anatomy Park, but given Rick's frustration that it won't include a "Pirates of the Pancreas", that may not be permanent. The replacement dimension version of him was later seen in "The Whirly Dirly Conspiracy". Body Horror:Morty uses the Morphizer-XE to horribly mutilate him for dumping Summer and breaking her heart. Dark and Troubled Past: Ethan was molested by his older brother on a fishing trip. Disproportionate Retribution: SeeBody Horrorabove.Morty basically dooms him to a lifetime of pain and despair, because he dumped Summer and made her insecure about her body, and there is absolutely no indication that he will ever revert to his normal self. And by all appearances, Morty also left Ethan stranded at the campsite, forcing him to haul his malformed body all the way back to civilization on his own; judging by his pace during the after-credits scene, this might take some time. Drama Queen: In his initial appearance in C-137, he crashes the Smith family's Christmas dinner to ask Summer why she hasn't been texting him.

characters.name: Brad K.
characters.description: A student at Harry Herpson High School. He is a jock who plays football for the school and dates Jessica. Buffy Speak: He once tells Jessica that if she wants good words she should date a "languager." Jerk Jock: Plays football and bullies Morty. He is even somewhat self-aware about his role:Brad:(to Morty after he awkwardly tries to chat up Jessica)Dude, stay in your league! Look at how hot she is. You don't see me going to a bigger school in a wealthier district and hitting on their prettiest girl!Jessica:(rolls her eyes)Gee,thanks, Brad.Brad:I throw balls far. You want good words? Date a languager.

characters.name: Nancy P.
characters.description: A nerd girl with whom Summer is friends with. They share the same flute class. Because of her nerd status, Summer denies their friendship when socializing with popular kids. Embarrassing Pyjamas: In "Rattlestar Ricklactica", Nancy is at Summer's place for sleepover with her and Tricia. When Summer puts on "snake jazz" and starts jamming with Tricia, Nancy asks about altering the course of a species without repercussions, prompting Summer to call Nancy a huge nerd and Tricia to insult Nancy's embarrassing candy-cane footy pajamas and her weight. The Friend Nobody Likes:Played With. She went with Summer to flute practice and the latter invited the former to her party, where Summer denied being friends with her, due to the popular girls not liking her. Though it's unknown how good the friendship between Summer and Nancy was at that point or if they were just acquaintances. Also, it's unknown how well Nancy gets along with her other friends if she even has any. Nevertheless, at least Squanchy respects her, considering he refused to let Summer at his place after Nancy told him how Summer treated her.

characters.name: Toby Matthews
characters.description: Yet another boy that Summer obsesses over. Ink-Suit Actor: He looks like a blond, slightly younger version of his voice actor.

characters.name: Tricia Lange
characters.description: A girl from Morty and Summer's high school that Summer's ex Ethan dumps her for. Buxom Beauty Standard: It's suggested more than once that Ethan dumped Summer for Tricia because the latter has big breasts. Summerends up so jealous of themshe tries to use one ofRicks's enlargement devices just to be able to compete. Casual Kink: She mentions enjoying getting peed on, and once described true love as intimate as docking. She's also weirdly turned on by watching Jerry keep bees, getting so aroused in the span of a minute or two that she eventually drops the pretense and just tells Summer she intends to sleep with Jerry. Ethical Slut: Initial portrayals make it seem like she's so nice that she's oblivious to how weird certain kinks are. Later on it becomes clear that however she got into it, she's actually so constantly horny that she ends up wanting to have sex with Jerry just by watching him keep some bees, and even goes as far as to drop the subtlety and tell Summer directly that she wants to rail him. Given Summer's reaction it seems she wasn't that surprised, meaning she might be used to Tricia being up for sleeping with basically anyone. Likes Older Men: InThe Stingerof Promortyous, she slowly talks herself in wanting to have sex withJerry, right in front of Summer no less!

characters.name: Bruce Chutback
characters.description: A new kid at school whom everyone find cool. Morty and Summer tries to befriend him to not be seen as losers. Broken Pedestal: He is initially seems as a cool kid by Morty and Summer until they see how ungrateful he is and realize that they don't have to buy into his popularity. The same thing eventually happen to him with the whole school after he "embarrasses" himself. Dull Surprise: He reacts with very little emotions to out of the ordinaries things such as interdimensional TV or being sent to space and meeting aliens. Morty and Summer takes this as a sign of his superior coolness. Embarrassing Nickname: After one of the popular kids notices he wore the same pants two days in a row, he gets the nickname "Bruce Chutpants" and become the school's laughingstock. New Transfer Student: He is new at school. Meaning he hasn't anything embarrassing on his reputation yet. Making him cool.

characters.name: Davin
characters.description: Beth's co-worker, whom Jerry feels threatened by. Behavioral Transformation First: Rick's shenanigans lead to an outbreak of a virus that turns all of humanity (except the Smith-Sanchez family) into deformed mantis monsters that have a romantic obsession with Morty. Davin tries to hit on Beth before he catches the virus and suddenly starts asking her about her son's private parts. Body Horror: When Davin turns into a giant mantis, two large eyes burst from the sides of his head, straining against some threads of skin while a set of mandibles erupts from his mouth. The Bus Came Back: Davin is shown alive and well in "The Curicksous Case of Bethjamin Button", showing that in the Parmesean dimension the events of "Rick Potion #9" either never happened or were fixed before Jerry killed him. Dead Alternate Counterpart: In the "Rick Potion #9" Jerry beats a Cronenberged Davin to death with a crowbar.

characters.name: Mr. Meeseeks
characters.description: A race of creatures created from a box to fulfill simple goals. They do what is asked of them, and then abruptly cease to exist. They really don't like existing, so if the task given to them takes too long to accomplish, they may go insane and try to kill their summoner.They have aself-demonstrating page! Look at me! The Ace: Completed the comically difficult tasks Summer and Beth set them as if they were nothing and seem toknow how to do everything anyone could ask them to do from birth,the only thing they can't do is makeJerryany better at golf. This may be because dealing with Summer and Beth only required the Meeseeks to emotionally manipulate and/or convince others which they are very good at thanks to their unflinchingly upbeat personalities. Whereas Jerry wanted them to make him better at a physical task that required skill but was unwilling to actually change his behavior. Alien Blood: As shown during the fight scene in "Meeseeks and Destroy", their blood is white. Knowing how much the show indulges in Freudian symbolism, the seminal imagery might be intentional. And I Must Scream: Existence is pain to a Meeseeks and the longer they stay alive the greater their pain becomes, in the background of "Morty's Mindblowers" two Mr. Meeseeks are kept captive in a box forever with no task to complete, effectively forcing them to live forever. Ax-Crazy: If they can't finish their assigned task in a short enough amount of time, they'll summon more and more Meeseeks trying to solve the problem, start beating the pulp out of each other, and destroy everything in their path to get to and kill the person who assigned them theImpossible Taskso they can die.

characters.name: Gazorpians
characters.description: An alien race whose society segregates males and females due to the males supposedly being too savage. Abusive Alien Parents: Downplayed. Gazorpians raise female babies just fine but literally catapult male ones outside to live on their own. Their society justifies this because the males are shown to be incredibly violent and try to gang-rape Summer the moment they see her. Always Chaotic Evil: The male Gazorpians are considered the most violent, savage beings in the universe; evenHalf-Human HybridMorty Jr., who has human intelligence, was born with these tendencies. Female Gazorpians are more civilized, but are a species ofman-hatingdictators.Morty jr. was able to outgrow his savage impulses and becomes a prolific author, so in all likelihood the female Bazorpians just didn't have the patience to guide their male brethren into civilization. There's also a Gazorpian version ofGarfield, who is a jerkass to his Jon but otherwise non-violent, which further suggests Gazorpians can channel their emotions into works of fiction when given proper guidance. Morty jr. was able to outgrow his savage impulses and becomes a prolific author, so in all likelihood the female Bazorpians just didn't have the patience to guide their male brethren into civilization. There's also a Gazorpian version ofGarfield, who is a jerkass to his Jon but otherwise non-violent, which further suggests Gazorpians can channel their emotions into works of fiction when given proper guidance. Attempted Rape: The first thing that happens to Summer upon arriving on Gazorpazorp, complete with a terrifyingPOVshot of her struggling to keep her legs from being pried open by the savage male Gazorpians. Thankfully, Rick kicks ass and saves her by killing them.

characters.name: Dr. Helen Wong
characters.description: An insightful family therapist who also specializes in treating coprophagia. After having incidents in school, Beth takes Morty and Summer to her, where she analyzes the family's dysfunctional relationship, particularly Beth's relationship with Rick and how it reflects in the family. Always Someone Better: The only character in the show, so far, to score a victory on Rick, in that she prevents the latter from getting in the last word. She does this by acknowledging Rick's great intelligence and even admitting that she understands why someone like him would mock and belittle her vocation but also pointing out that Rick can't handle life not being an adventure while she can. Awesome by Analysis: She was able immediately identify the root cause of Beth and her family's problems within a few seconds of speaking with them, and repeatedly uses this ability on the Smiths to reveal that they're not as good at hiding their problems as they think. Badass Normal: One of the few beings in the multiverse who can give Rick sensible and self-restricting advice that he will actually take, and who can firmly but calmly set boundaries in her relationship with him. Base-Breaking Character:In-Universe. The family literally is evenly split about her, with Beth and Rick disliking her and disregarding her advice while Morty and Summer are shown to have liked her and, especially considering everything they've been through, really would like her to help them. Averted in later episodes, which show that the entire family, Rick included, regularly go back to her and are working through their problems.

characters.name: Gene
characters.description: The Smith family's next-door neighbor. He tries to get along with them despite constantly getting caught in their chaotic antics. Butt-Monkey: Rarely does anything go right for him when he shows up in an episode. From getting yelled at by Morty when showing concern in a domestic dispute to being sexually propositioned by Rick's garage to getting his garden run over by Beth, he constantly bears the brunt of the Smith-Sanchez family's adventures. Expy: Introduced as a stand in for the Smith Family'sWilsonas the next door neighbor giving advice. The Friend Nobody Likes: He ends up roped into Mr. Poopybutthole's intervention in the season 7 premiere as the group's designated driver. The only person who treats him nicely isHugh Jackman, who turns out to be his cousin-in-law, and even he ends up forgetting about Gene while the group says their goodbyes at the end of the episode. A later episode has Birdperson tell Rick they need to remove him from their group chat. Major Injury Underreaction: In "The Curicksous Case Of Bethjamin Button", he has both his ankles sliced and his hand burned to the point the skin slides right off, exposing his bone, and he reacts to it surprisingly well. Justified as he's used to this being Rick's neighbor and Rick heals him back to normal when he can.

characters.name: Ice-T/Water-T/Magma-T
characters.description: Ice-T, one of Earth's most famous rappers. It turns out he's actually an alien from the planet Alphabetrium, a planet where everyone is a letter of the alphabet. Originally named Water-T, he was turned to ice and exiled from his homeworld by his father, Magma-Q, for not caring enough about others. Actor Allusion: His father, Magma-Q, is voiced byIce-T. Beethoven Was an Alien Spy: Who knew that one of the most prominent rappers happens to be an alien prince? Changed My Mind, Kid: He returns to protect the Earth from the Cromulons in order to let Rick and Morty perform their song. Dating Catwoman: He over the course of his second appearance he starts a relationship and eventually marries a member of the Numbericons, a race his people had been in aForever Warwith.

characters.name: Tophat Jones
characters.description: The mascot forStrawberry Smigglesbreakfast cereal, Tophat Jones is a leprechaun-like being who hoards all the Strawberry Smiggles for himself, only to meet a gruesome demise at the hands of the children his cereal is intended for. Disproportionate Retribution: Tries to keep all the cereal to himself like the Real Life mascots he parodies, but instead of just losing the cereal, he's brutally murdered for it. Dragged Off to Hell: Implied at the end where he begs Jesus to take him away in the moments of his death, only to claim that he's seeing demons approaching. Expy: OfLucky Charmsmascot Lucky the Leprechaun. His rabbit ears also call to mind the Trix Rabbit. Family-Unfriendly Death: Has his stomach carved open by the children and its contents devoured.

characters.name: Ants-In-My-Eyes Johnson
characters.description: The owner of "Ants-In-My-Eyes Johnson's Electronics", an outlet store for home appliances on an alternate Earth. Like his name indicates, Johnson has hundreds of ants crawling around on his eyeballs, keeping him from seeing anything, but it doesn't seem to bother him too much, possibly because of a second ailment — a malfunctioning nervous system that keeps him from feeling anything on his body. Eye Scream: Ohgodyes, the ants don't seem to do any actual damage, but the very idea of having insects crawling on your eyeballs is bad enough. Honest John's Dealership: Averted, his shop seems to be reasonably normal, not counting the bizarre nature of its owner. Major Injury Underreaction: You'd think being mostly blind and unable to feel anything would be anAnd I Must Screamscenario, but Johnson doesn't seem to mind his living situation too much. Man on Fire: He sets himself on fire with a gas stove and doesn't notice due to his lack of sensation.

characters.name: Abradolf Lincler
characters.description: An experiment created when Rick combined the DNA of Abraham Lincoln and Adolf Hitler, in an attempt to create a morally neutral super leader... what resulted was an awkward being of ambiguous moral standings. Adolf Hitlarious: He's a partial clone of Adolf Hitler who is completely ineffectual and played for humor. Badass Boast: "Prepare to be emancipated from your own inferior genes!" Godwin's Law of Facial Hair: He is a fusion of Adolf Hitler and Abraham Lincoln Rick made in an attempt to make a morally neutral superleader. However, the experiment fails and Abrodolph gets into a fight at a party after referring to a black partygoer as "boy". Heroic Sacrifice: To protect Morty and Summer's friend from a two-headed monster while they gathered crystals.He got better, although he suffersA Fate Worse Than Death.

characters.name: Shrimply Pibbles
characters.description: The galaxy's most influential civil rights leader. All-Loving Hero: He devoted his life to civil rights.Pibbles: "Kindness is the currency of the universe, consider donating today." Bizarre Alien Biology: He needs heroin to live and the human penis can be implanted in his body as a replacement heart. Doomed Hometown: His home planet was the target of a genocide and utterly destroyed. Expy: A combination of Gandhi and the Dalai Lama.

characters.name: The Eyehole Man
characters.description: An alien wearing a purple superhero cape and mask. He's the mascot forEye Holesbrand cereal, appearing in one of the segments of "Interdimensional Cable Part 2", who brutally assaults anyone he catches with a box of his Eyeholes, insisting that he's the only one allowed to have Eyeholes. As Jerry finds out inThe Stingerfor this episode, that is not an idle threat. The Dreaded: Anyone who eats from a box of Eyeholes runs the risk of getting attacked by the Eyehole Man, no matter what planet they're on. Rick tells Morty to keep his eye out. Expy: Basically a mascot like the Trix Rabbit or Lucky The Leprechaun taken to a logical extreme. Jerkass: He's a highly aggressive asshole who unhesitatingly beats the tar out of anyone he catches with his cereal for the sole reason that he doesn't want anyone besides himself to have it. No-Holds-Barred Beatdown: What happens if the Eyehole Man catches you eating his Eyeholes, he comes crashing in through a window and just starts beating the everloving crap out of you.

characters.name: Stealy
characters.description: A strange alien creature who hosts a show called "The Adventures of Stealy" on "Interdimensional Cable" which features him going to different locations and stealing random things, then rating them in his secret hideout to show how much they're worth. Bag of Holding: Can hold a surprising amount of loot in the pockets of his vest. Impossible Thief: Averted, he snatches whatever catches his eye, and the people he steals from occasionally notice him but tend to be so baffled by the bizarre sight that they dont react. If they do protest, Stealy just pulls out a rag full of chloroform and drugs them. Sticky Fingers: The entire point of his show, he'll steal literallyanything, valuable or not. Rubber Man: Has very long, rubber-like arms.

characters.name: Arthricia
characters.description: ACat Girlfrom an alien planet. She is rescued from the Purge by Rick and Morty. She secretly plans on killing the aristocrats who organize the purge. Action Girl: She can be quite deadly when given access to proper weaponry. All for Nothing: Her goal in killing the planet's elites was to put a stop to the yearly purging festival once and for all, but the other survivors decide they would rather just keep it going to work out their pent up aggression. All Love Is Unrequited: Morty likes her (or at least that is what she thought he was going to say when he wanted to ask her a question), but she doesn't reciprocate. She claims to already have a boyfriend, but the way she says it seems to imply that she's lying and is just not interested in him. Bad Liar: Very awkwardly claims she to have a boyfriend when Morty asks her out. Eventually, Morty feels so patronised he just tells her to knock it off.

characters.name: Hemorrhage
characters.description: The brutal leader of a wasteland gang. He is a nihilist who shares chemistry with Summer. The Apunkalypse: Like everyone in his gang apparently. Bucket Helmet: His main headgear is a bucket painted with a skull. Cool Helmet: He uses apainted bucketthat hideshis incredibly plain appearance: a normal-looking blonde guy with a somewhat thin mustache. Expy: He's a parody of Lord Humungus fromMad Max 2: The Road Warrior.

characters.name: Kiara
characters.description: A Krutabulon warrior priestess Jerry hooks up with on an interstellar dating service Rick mentioned. Action Girl: Par for the course given that she's both a warrior priestess and voiced byJennifer Hale. Action Girlfriend: To Jerry. Exotic Equipment: Jerry implies she has two vaginas. Fantastic Racism: Her people seem to despise and go to great lengths to exterminate the varrix, which are initially depicted as being like mindless vermin, but turn out to be completely sapient.

characters.name: Joseph Eli Lipnip
characters.description: Tommy's father. He was wrongly convicted of murdering and eating his son and was almost executed for it before Beth saved him. Acquitted Too Late:NarrowlyAverted. He was acquitted just before the lethal injection was administered. A second later and he'd be dead. Clear Their Name: Beth clears his name by bringing Tommy's cloneto the prison, proving that he didn't eat his son. Earn Your Happy Ending: Is reunited with his wife and witha clone ofhis beloved son, after being wrongly imprisoned for thirty years and almost executed. Gunman with Three Names: Although he isn't accused of using a gun.

characters.name: Glootie
characters.description: An alien that Rick hired, or possibly enslaved, to work as his intern. He also tattooed "Do Not Develop His App" on Glootie's forehead, and for good reason as it turns out. Affably Evil: Always cheerful, helpful and polite, even after his true plans are revealed. Catchphrase: "Do you wanna develop an app?", which he manages to drop about five times in the span of thirty seconds in his first appearance The Cobbler's Children Have No Shoes: Despite his species having allegedly "perfected" romantic relationships, the Love Finderrz app can't find any soulmate matches for Glootie. The only other person this is seen happening to is Jerry. Dead Man's Switch: When Morty and Jerry try to force him to turn off the app, he activates what seems to be one of these,but it's actually just an app on his phone that beeps and glows, so he can escape when his attackers take cover. He's a bit too portly and slow to get away in time.

characters.name: Tony
characters.description: A widower that uses Rick's secret toilet, and becomes the target of his ire. Alien Blood: His people seem to have mauve blood, as shown when Rick punches another version of Tony in the face. The Anti-Nihilist: Leans into this after crossing paths with Rick. He accepts that the universe will keep on taking things away and obsessing over the few things you think you can control won't change that. All the while, Rick obsesses over someone whoused his toilet. Foil: To Rick. Both are men coping with past losses, but while Rick reacts to the uncaring void of the universe in mostly destructive or obsessive ways, Tony learns to take it in stride and is inspired to enjoy his fleeting life. He goes on to die shortly afterwards while committing to his newfound love of life, leaving behind friends and a loving family to mourn him. Meanwhile Rick has countless back-up plans to protect himself from death even in old age, and struggles with his relationships with his family. Killed Offscreen: The secretary of his job informs Rick that Tony died skiing down Space Mt. Everest.

characters.name: The Glorzos
characters.description: A species of parasitic beings that take over their hosts and reproduce by generating an egg that kills them and the host when created. Rick, Morty and Summer are taken in by them, with Rick and Morty being taken over by some parasites. Alien Blood: Their blood is greenish-yellow Aliens Are Bastards: Subverted. Parasitic life-cycle aside, they aren't malicious beings. They only wanted to use Rick's technology to explore the universe, and their intercoms preach of peace. Artistic License – Biology: A reproductive process wherein the organism produces only a single egg and immediately dies completely defeats the purpose, since it does not provide a net population increase and thus does not help to replace idividuals who die from other causes, dooming the species to eventual extinction. Everyone Has Standards: When Rick's parasite makes a series of internet videos saying that their hosts only exist to spawn more of them, a large number of glorzos frown on his narrow-minded attitude.It's clearly meant to evoke YouTubers that make conspiracy commentary, with a particular reference to Alex Jones and his side business of selling Brain Power pills.That said, he was only lashing out about biological drives because he wanted to start a family with Morty's facehugger, who became favored by Summer and began to neglect him.

characters.name: Mr. Always Wants to be Hunted
characters.description: A starfish man in a target suit who always wants to be hunted. Berserk Button: Being ignored is a major one for him, as he murders one of the Smith-Sanchez decoy families just because they didn't hunt him. Beware the Silly Ones: He looks like a starfish wearing a black-and-white striped jumpsuit with a bullseye on it, whose only goal is to be hunted. He seems like a ridiculous gag character who's only around for a quick laugh, but when people don't hunt him, he hunts them in revenge. Chekhov's Gunman: He seems like just a one-note character around for a quick gag in theCold Openand then is discarded once the actual plot is set in motion. At the end of the episode he returns and murders the remaining decoy family because nobody hunted him, even though that family wasn't the same one that ignored him. Disproportionate Retribution: When one decoy family of Smith-Sanchezs stops hunting him to deal with the squids trying to kill them, Mr. Always Wants to be Hunted shows up at the end and guns down the remaining Smith-Sanchez decoy family (different than the one that ignored him) because nobody hunted him.

characters.name: Blazen
characters.description: A katana-wielding mercenary tasked with fighting Morty's sperm. Heroes Prefer Swords: Uses a katana whereas all the other mooks use guns. Doesn't do him much good in the end though. Paper Tiger: He's established as the coolest looking character on the team assigned to exterminate Morty's mutant sperm. He quickly blows his whole image in his big moment. First his katana gets stuck in the ceiling of a cave, then when he jumps to grab it his pants drop and everyone sees he's wearing women's underwear. The katana then drops out on its own, impaling Blazen. His dying wish is for Rick and Morty to find his wife, who he claims is Kathy Ireland. They assume he's delusional, but the the real Kathy Ireland shows up and confirms they were married. Then when she hears that he was wearing her underwear she's repulsed.

characters.name: Changeformers
characters.description: Robots that change into vehicles. Does This Remind You of Anything?: The Changeformers berate and belittle Rick's Car after losing her disguise, calling her a "Just-Car". The fact that one is sodisgusted, he throws up on her may be on par with blatant transphobia. Expy: Of theTransformers, naturally. Fantastic Racism: When the Changeformers realize that Rick's Car is just a sentient car and not a Changeformer herself, the one who was hitting on her is so disgusted hevomits all over heras they all mock her. Hold Your Hippogriffs: One of the Changeformers' last words are "Oh, the Changeformity!".

characters.name: Coop
characters.description: A marine who willingly transforms into a turkey as part of the President's secret mission to stop Rick Sanchez from getting a Presidential turkey pardon on Thanksgiving. Failed a Spot Check: Failed to realize that two of his turkified soldiers had been replaced by Rick and Morty, or that the turkey they're rescuing isn't the President but a random turkey that swallowed his tracking pill. Good Ol' Boy: He's just a simple country boy man who wants his future race car driver son to grow up in a world where he can fill his pickup with hot dogs and drive it to a juke box playing their demographic's current favorite music. Emphasized by his voice actor using the same Eastern Kentucky drawl he used forRaylan Givens. My Girl Back Home: His pregnant wife, Mary Lou, who keeps trying, in vain, to talk Coop out of risking his life on increasingly absurd missions. No Good Deed Goes Unpunished: His reward for helping the President save the world from Turkey President? PTSD from his time spent transformed as a turkey and his healthcare taken away by his boss to buy more missiles.

characters.name: Memory Tammy
characters.description: A memory of Tammy from Birdperson's mind. Since she's a memory from back when Birdperson thought she was a good person who loved him, she acts like the person he thought she was rather than the evil individual she was in real-life. Dying Declaration of Love: She tells Birdperson she loves him just before she's wiped from existence in his decaying dreamscape. Evil Me Scares Me: Given that she's a memory from before her true personality was revealed, she's understandably disturbed to see the memory versions of herself who killed BP and resurrected him as a cyborg. Face Death with Dignity: Having told Birdperson she loves him one last time, she watches him escape his crumbling mind and calmly embraces oblivion with a peaceful look andsmileon her face. Locked Out of the Loop: She's a memory who only knows what Birdperson knows and a lot of his memories are locked away by Federation brainalyzer technology. As such, she's just as surprised as Birdperson is when told thatthey have a child.

characters.name: Crow Aliens
characters.description: A race of beings that evolved from corvids. Expy: The Crow Aliens are modeled after the Skeksis fromThe Dark Crystal. Higher-Tech Species: The crow aliens vastly outclass Rick in terms of technology, capturing him in an inescapable tractor beam when he dumps two crows on their planet and actually manage to teach him empathy. Uplifted Animal: The crow aliens being sapient humanoids is independent from them being aliens, as they acquired their form and intelligence from a giant glowing artifact resembling a hatched egg.

characters.name: Old M. Hucksbee
characters.description: An employee of Fortune 500, tasked with making the fortunes in the cookies. Bestiality Is Depraved: Besides escaping from the factory, he also wants to have sex with the Lockerean creature. Cruel and Unusual Death: He gets torn apart limb-by-limb by the Lockerean creature. Face Death with Dignity: Upon realizing the alien creature he loved was nothing more than a wild animal, his only response was to deliver an anecdote about the nature of interspecies sex, and then says "Well, joopidty-boop, time to die." before being torn apart by an alien creature. Half-Witted Hillbilly: Of the Country Bumpkin type. He is certainly a parody of a redneck.

characters.name: The Lockerean
characters.description: A creature whose fecal matter has the power to influence destiny. The Dog Bites Back: Once the Lockerean—who, as lampshaded by Hucksbee, is basically a wild animal held captive against its will—is freed from its restraints, it's quick to maul and kill pretty much everyone it encounters, many of whom are at least partially responsible for holding it captive, like the remainder of the guards and Jennith. It also rips apart Hucksbee himself,not that he minds too much. Literal Genie: The fortunes do exactly what the message specifies and nothing else. Get immortality? Doesn't mean you're invincible. Control over water? The water has to come from somewhere (people, in this case). Misfortune Cookie: Jerry gets a fortune cookie saying he will have sex with his mother. Hucksbee explains he deliberately makes these types of fortunes in the hopes someone would come to the factory to investigate and help him. Monster Organ Trafficking: Its species eats chaos, but it has a digestive disorder that allows its poop to be consumed to manipulate entropy. Its poop comes out as empty fortune cookies which make whatever fortune placed inside them inevitable.

characters.name: The Dinosaurs
characters.description: Three Dinosaurs consisting of aTyrannosaurus rex, aBrachiosaurusand aTriceratopswho return to Earth to find it inhabited by humans. They are benevolent though oblivious to human nature, and bid to turn the Earth into aUtopia, but swiftly get sent away from Earth due to circumstances beyond them.... All for Nothing: The dinosaurs, to their immense sorrow, realize that their efforts are for naught because every utopia they usher in inevitably attracts malicious living meteors that destroy the worlds they uplifted. They, and Rick, even drop the trope name word-for-word. Alternate-History Dinosaur Survival: It turns out the dinosaurs did not all go extinct, but a handful left such as this trio for outer space and came back to Earth after some 66 million years. Always Someone Better:Zig-Zagged. Rick casually proclaims himself on the same level as the dinosaurs, but though they don't brag about it, they seemingly prove him wrong with their far superior technology. They even have portal technology and traveled the multiverse, before deciding to focus on their universe of origin. However, Rick very quickly understands their tech and adapts his own to counter it, to the point that in the episode's climax the Dinosaurs are powerless to move him away against his will. Balance of Good and Evil: The show gives aScience Fictionversion of the concept with these dinosaurs and the sentient meteors. While the dinosaurs evolved into "higher and higher levels of loving vegan godhood, another life-form devolved into an equally selfless hate-filled species of barely-sentient rocks" that seek out the dinosaurs as a form ofAnimal Jingoism, crashing into every planet that the dinosaurs colonize.

characters.name: Gul'Karna
characters.description: A Predator whom Mr. Poopybutthole hired as a private investigator to keep tabs on his ex-wife Amy only for him to sleep with her instead. Et Tu, Brute?: Mr. Poopybutthole was not pleased to find out the guy he hired to watch over his ex-wife ends up sleeping with her. Good Stepfather: He goes fullPapa Wolfwhen Mr. Poppybutthole kidnaps Poopy Jr.; Poopy Jr. cries at seeing him getting beaten up and Amy tells her ex-husband that she, her son, and Gul'Karna are now a family. Names to Run Away from Really Fast: His full name/title is "Gul'Karna, Clan Leader of the Skin-Thieves". Predator Pastiche: Subverted, he's just literally a Predator from the film series of the same name, complete with all of the weapons, the green blood, etc. One wonders if his appearance was an officially-sanctioned crossover, since he's really not a "parody" outside of appearing in a comedic context.

characters.name: Fred Bunks
characters.description: A terminally ill widower from 41 Kepler B. Character Tics: Has been eating jam with his fingers since childhood. During his time with Amber the two shared in this quirk. Childhood Friends: He and Amber have known each other since they were children. Earn Your Happy Ending: Fred's dreams of becoming an architect failed due to his inability to keep up in class, his relationship with Amber crashed and burned with little chance of recovery, he turned to drugs, alcohol and meaningless sex as a coping mechanism and his parents died shortly after he was forced to move back in with them. When Fred decides to create Fredblox and market it as a toy, his life turns around once more, he cleans up his act and Amber falls in love with him again. Amber spends the rest of her life with Fred. The Everyman: His life's story reveals him to be a standard middle-class guy who experienced various highs and lows. The fact that Fred's history was so relatable is what ultimately decides the market for suicide spaghetti.

characters.name: Amber
characters.description: Fred's love interest. Childhood Friends: She and Fred have known each other since they were children. Connected All Along: For a time, Amber was married to the man that Rick had harvested for suicide spaghetti at the start of the episode. Hairstyle Inertia: Ever since childhood her hair has been styled into a pair of short bushy ponytails, with the only variant being when she added purple highlights during her teen-young adult years. Parental Abandonment: After she rekindled things with Fred, she left her husband and her kids.

characters.name: Mrs. Mobius
characters.description: The wife of Rick's friend Slow Mobius, introduced after he was killed by Rick Prime. Bait-and-Switch:The Stingerhas Slow Mobius' wife go through depression after he iserased from all infinite timelinesby the Omega Device, with her eventually setting out on a journey to apparently hunt down his killer like Rick did after Rick Prime killed his family — complete with the same melancholy synth music played over his flashback in "Rickmurai Jack" — a task doomed to fail since Rick Prime is already dead. Instead, she meets an alien who is going through something similar after the death of his own wife and the two bond, dropping their quests for revenge and instead raising their families together as each other'sSecond Love, all while the background music changes to become happier and more hopeful. Cycle of Revenge: Defied. Slow Mobius ends up getting killed by Rick Prime's Omega Device, whicherases him from all infinite timelines. His wife still remembers him, and swears to take revenge, eventually going through the samejourney to seek out information, until she meets another person who is also going through the exact same journey, which convinces both of them to settle down and raise their families together. Her Heart Will Go On: Slow Mobius's wife manages to move on from his death in the post-credits scene thanks to her finding aSecond Love. Ironic Echo: Slow Mobius' wife goes through the samejourney to seek out informationon who killed her husband in the same way thatRick did to find Rick Prime after Diane's death. Thankfully, her story hasa happier ending.

characters.name: Churry
characters.description: A churro that Morty had Rick turn into a living being. Animate Inanimate Object: Deconstructed; One adventure is Morty having Rick animate a churro for him to have as a friend. When Morty comes back to Rick asking to make Churry a normal churro again, Rick explainsthat to bring Churry to life without needing any internal organs he had to make him functionally immortal; he can't turn him back into a normal churro. Morty, not happy to learn this, abandons Churry on a barren planet, which leads him to swear vengeance. A Lizard Named "Liz": A churro named Churry. Morty's not the best at naming things. The Thing That Would Not Leave: Implied to be how Morty ends up feeling about the idea of Churry being immortal and staying by his sideforever, even though he does enjoy hanging out with Churry. The clip was used as evidence to show how immoral and fickle Morty could be after all.

characters.name: Sinistar- 7
characters.description: A Numbericon that finds herself allied with Water-T. Abusive Parents: Her father Lord Dreadnought didn't think twice about punishing her incompetence with force lightning. Anthropomorphic Typography: A sentient number. Belligerent Sexual Tension: Water-T and Sinistar 7 start out as enemies, then move into this after the former saves the latter from drowning, eventually leading to them making out. By the end, once their two civilizations have merged, they've become anOfficial Couple. Big "NO!": Sinistar 7 delivers one when Water-T's group escapes her pursuit, as well as when Infinity kills her father.

characters.name: Reinhard Kincaid
characters.description: A member of a religious militia called the Christ Troopers whose mission is to purge the universe of sexual content. Awful Wedded Life: Reinhard goes back home, having to crawl to the front door due tohaving his lower body torn off, only for his wife to chew him out with zero concern for his horrific injury before slamming the door in his face. As noted, they apparently refuse to have sex with each other in spite of their marital status. Big Damn Heroes: Exaggerated with Reinhard saving the day at the last moment even though he's missing his lower body and last seen left all the way back on Easter Island. Apparently, he crawled to one of the island's head ships and flew over, only to land a fair distance away and take a bus to the Smith's house within the space of a minute. Didn't Think This Through: Reinhard comes back to his wife hoping to have sex with her after his harrowing mission changed his mind about sex. However, he didn't consider that 1) his wife was raised to hate sex just like he was and, unlike him, hasn't had any reason to change her mind, and 2) he literally can't do so because he's got no pelvis. After she predictably rejects him, he lampshades that he's lived his life poorly. Five-Second Foreshadowing: When Reinhard finally unmasks himself, the audience will almost certainly notice his resemblance to the typical pop culture Jesus. He reveals in short order that the person known on Earth as Jesus was a member of his order who was sent to Earth to kill the Easter Bunny, only for humanity to crucify him instead.Morty:Woah, that isnothow we tell that story.

characters.name: Doug and Karen Jamerson
characters.description: Two upper-class passengers aboard theSleeper Starshipthat Rick and Morty tried to loot. Due to some confusion, they mistake Rick for an aged-up version of their son. Because You Were Nice to Me: Rick takes a shine to Karen and Doug Jamerson when they, mistaking him for their son Jimmy, act like kind, loving parents to him. He even goes out of his way to rescue them during the Makey rebellion, and later directly states this.Rick: They were nice, so I was nice back! Try it sometime,Morty! Innocently Insensitive: As nice as they are, Karen and Doug don't fully understand just how privileged their wealth really makes them or how economically imbalanced their society (consisting of lower-class, indentured laborers "Makeys" and upper-class "Takeys", to which Karen and Doug belong) is, and it's all but stated through Doug's dialogue that they're the reason why Jimmy is such a spoiled brat.

characters.name: Cogs
characters.description: Clairvoyant kitchenstaff at an intergalactic restaurant. Bald Mystic: Standard for science-fiction psychics, none of them have hair on their oversized craniums. The Chessmaster: Naturally as clairvoyants they pull off a successful gambit that involves manipulating Summer and Rick emotionally to get what they want. Creepy Blue Eyes: They have pale blue irides, which establishes that they're not human as no human characers in this series have irides. The Dividual: They are not referred to individually by Rick or Summer, only collectively called "it".

characters.name: Mups
characters.description: An alien race that Snowball and his followers genitically altered into domesticated pets. City Mouse: Invoked for a gag. The Mancors blame the Mups' disastrous use of weapons on "city living". Genetic Abomination: They are grotesque humanoid creatures bred by the dog society through selective genetics and post-birth modification, customizable via "drag-and-drop" before or after birth once "the stitch is healed." The Grotesque: They are grotesque in nature in several varying degrees and wouldn't look out of place in Beth's altered Froopy Land.

characters.name: Mancors
characters.description: A species indigenous to Snowball's colonized planet that feuds with the dogs. La Résistance: The Mancors are group of Mups which managed to escape into the wild and are planning an uprising. One-Word Vocabulary: All they can say is "Take, take, take". Except for their leader. You Are in Command Now: Morty is kidnapped by the Mancors and taken to join their resistance against their dog oppressors. Despite Morty insisting he wants nothing to do with their revolution, their leader gets killed by a Dog attack and she designates Morty as her successor. Left with no other choice, Morty decides to lead the Mancors against the Dogs if only so he could get revenge on Snowball for trying to kill him.

characters.name: Professor Tock
characters.description: A time detective who has a history with Rick, and investigates him and Morty during their future stock scheme. Doctor Whomage: Of the Doctor fromDoctor Whothough more specifically to the older Doctors. He strongly resembles theFirst Doctorif he stole the multi-colored clothes of theSixth Doctor. Hero Antagonist: Morty thinks he's an all right dude, and we learn that he iscompletelyjustified in taking down Rick. Inspector Javert: Subverted. Tock immediately assumes that Rick is up to no good when he shows up at the stock exchange. Justified, sinceRick is... well Rickand his stock scheme has the side effect of destroying parallel universes. Pungeon Master: Repeatedly makes lame puns related to time and clocks, much to Rick's annoyance.

characters.name: Morty 304-X
characters.description: The Morty hailing from the only universe where Rick never existed. Started out as a kid genius who developed amazing technologies, but he becameDrunk with Powerand turned his world into aCyberpunkdystopia. He sets his sights on systematically exterminating the Ricks and conquering the multiverse. Batman Gambit: Sends out the killer blob to hunt down Ricks with the expectation that any Rick would come to his dimension, whom he could then capture and force to help him master interdimensional travel. Became Their Own Antithesis: Actually fled from a world destroyed by his Rick, accompanied by his Summer, Beth, and Jerry, and settled in Universe 304-X specifically so they would no longer have to deal with a Rick. But something in Universe 304-X made Morty more intelligent and cruel, sending him down a warped path similar to Rick's. Body Horror: Something happened which heavily scarred his face, though we are not shown exactly what. Broken Ace: According to 304-X Summer, this Morty was a bona fide scientific genius until the omnipotent power his inventions afforded him went to his head. Becomes a subversion when it turns out he's more of a case of"Flowers for Algernon" Syndromethan someone who started out an Ace.

characters.name: Peacock Jones
characters.description: A self-styled alien adventurer who travels the cosmos with a succession of female companions, whom he takes along solely for sexual favors. He becomes infatuated with Summer and takes her on as his new companion with the intention of getting into her pants. Later joins Party Dog's Rick Revenge Squad. Brainwashing: The end of Issue #58 reveals that, when Jones captured Morty, he didn'tphysicallyharm him...because he was doing this instead, using subliminal messaging in the TV show that he had Morty watch to brainwash Morty to kill Rick. The Bus Came Back:Returns in Issue #41 as a member of the Rick Revenge Squad. He ends up being the only member of the Squad who doesn't die, and manages to escape after Summer and Beth defeat him.Comes back again in Issue #56, working with theIllumiRickito get revenge on Rick. Returns in Issue #41 as a member of the Rick Revenge Squad. He ends up being the only member of the Squad who doesn't die, and manages to escape after Summer and Beth defeat him. Comes back again in Issue #56, working with theIllumiRickito get revenge on Rick.

characters.name: Mr. Sick
characters.description: A Meeseeks created by Rick to use as his drug mule when he was running a universal crime ring. Was eventually pinned for Rick's crimes and locked up with Peacock Jones, his existence becoming drawn out by not having his task completed. Later joins the Rick Revenge Squad, but disappears/"dies" when Rick defeats him by causing him to accomplish his intended purpose.

characters.name: Jerry J19ζ 7 aka Doofus Jerry
characters.description: The Jerry from Rick J19ζ7's dimension. In the same way that Rick J19ζ7 is the onlyNice Guyout of all the Ricks in the multiverse, Jerry J19ζ7 the only Jerry who is smart, wealthy... and ruthless. When he inadvertently learns about interdimensional travel thanks to Rick J19ζ7 and Comicsverse Jerry, he sets out to take over the the rest of the multiverse. The Ace: As an Opposite Jerry, he is confident, ambitious and naturally successful in anything he does, up to being capable of single-handedly conquering the Council of Ricks. He is only defeated due to Main Jerry accidentally summoning a giant worm after vomiting out some portal juice. Ambition Is Evil: This Jerry is driven by a desire for conqest, meaning he will stop at nothing short of complete domination of the multiverse. Arc Villain: He is the main antagonist of a short arc. The Casanova: An evil variation. As the most successful and powerful man of his own dimension, he has his own harem of women and they don't seem too unhappy with their situation. Later on, he even has a harem of Beths from multiple different dimensions.

characters.name: Krombopulos Amy
characters.description: Ascended Extra: In the show, she appeared very briefly during Krombopulos Michael's montage (during their wedding) in "Mortynight Run." In the comics, her story spans a few issues. Killed Offscreen: After Rick talks her down from killing Morty, he indicates behind her back that he wants Morty to shoot her, and the two later return without her (and it's stated in Issue #56 that Peacock was the only survivor of the Squad). Start of Darkness: Michael's death causes her to take up his trade with the single goal of killing Rick and Morty. Would Hurt a Child: Or, specifically, Morty, since he was the one who caused Michael's death.

characters.name: Party Dog
characters.description: The Bus Came Back: Not him, but rather, the one who defeats him. After the entire Smith-Sanchez family expresses their unwillingness to kill a dog (even one as brutal and ruthless as Party Dog), Rick jumps dimensions and summons Snuffles/Snowball to take care of the problem. Expy: Of 1980s Budweiser mascot SpudsMacKenzie. Mister Big: Is a fairly small dog, but is well known throughout the galaxy as a ruthless gangster. Non-Action Big Bad: He's never shown personally fighting, and instead commands his underlings or the Rick Revenge Squad to do his dirty work.

characters.name: Boon
characters.description: Badbutt: Rick notes that his catchphrasewas altered to sound less blasphemous. Rick also notes that since superhero franchises lack the balls (pun intended), any damage he'll do will be retconned for the sake of mass appeal.
